suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point managed gateways/agents for bulk policy changes, rule modifications, or agent uninstalls originating from a single admin token/session ID. Alert on administrator API calls that target 20+ gateways within minutes, which would indicate mass compromise or lateral movement across the managed firewall estate.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Scanner Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry means 'currently being exploited'; pipeline should surface attempts to exploit this specific CVE in real-time, not just patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole application logs and reverse-proxy logs for payloads known to trigger CVE-2026-16232 (specific API endpoint + malformed request, if public PoC released). Look for 401/403 followed by successful API calls without re-authentication, rapid authentication retry loops, or token-issuing API calls preceded by unauthenticated requests. Correlate with IDS/WAF alerts for known CVE-2026-16232 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect n8n Process Spawning Command Interpreters
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'Lets Workflow Editors Run OS Commands as the n8n Process'—any shell spawn (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) from n8n binary is direct exploitation indicator or malicious workflow execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent process matches n8n service binary. Flag spawning of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, /bin/sh, sh, csh) or system utilities (whoami, curl, nc, netcat). Establish baseline for legitimate workflow integrations and escalate deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Workflow Code Injection via API or File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Sandbox escape exploitation requires injecting malicious code into workflow definitions. Article implies 'Workflow Editors' trigger the escape—monitor workflow creation/modification API calls and file writes containing shell syntax or process invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor n8n workflow definition files or API audit logs for updates containing suspicious patterns: embedded shell commands (${...}, exec, eval), process invocation keywords, or base64-encoded payloads. Alert on non-standard nodes or expressions executing system calls. Correlate write events with user identity.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized File System Access from n8n Context
suggestion.rationale: Sandbox escape enables the process to access files beyond intended scope. Monitor n8n process reading/writing credential stores, configuration files, or parent directories outside its working directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of n8n file access patterns. Alert on reads from /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, SAM registry, browser credential stores, SSH keys, or API token files. Flag directory traversal attempts or access to system-level directories (/etc, /opt, C:\\Windows\\System32).

suggestion.title: Detect Privilege Escalation from n8n Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: If n8n runs with elevated privileges or sandbox escape allows token manipulation, attackers escalate from workflow editor to admin. Monitor for privilege escalation techniques initiated from n8n spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token impersonation, access token duplication, or UAC bypass attempts from n8n child processes. Alert when n8n spawns processes requesting higher privileges than parent. Cross-reference process creation with privilege escalation events and user account context.

suggestion.title: Detect n8n Process Establishing Unexpected Network Connections
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation of sandbox escape typically includes C2 beaconing or data exfiltration. Monitor n8n process for connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, suspicious ports, or known malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected n8n egress (API calls to legitimate SaaS integrations). Alert on connections to external IPs not in whitelist, non-standard ports (4444, 5555, 8888, 9999), or known C2 domains. Correlate with workflow execution timestamps to identify payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Workflow Execution Frequency and Timing
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation triggers malicious workflows—detect unusual execution frequency, concurrent runs, or execution outside business hours indicating automated compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor n8n execution logs for anomalies: execution outside user's active hours, bulk parallel executions, rapid retry loops, or execution by service account outside normal patterns. Alert on failed authentication followed by workflow execution (compromised credentials). Correlate with API key rotation or credential reset events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Vulnerable Driver Loading (BYOVD Exploit Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article names BYOVD as a core evasion technique; pipeline extracted nothing. BYOVD involves loading legitimate-but-vulnerable drivers to escalate or bypass security controls. Detection hypothesis should target unusual driver loads from non-system directories or unsigned driver loads with suspicious parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or out-of-policy driver loads (*.sys files) from temporary, user-writable, or unusual directories. Correlate with process execution from same directory tree or spawned by crypter-staging processes (dropped by initial payload). Flag when legitimate driver names are loaded from non-Windows\System32 paths.

suggestion.title: Process Ghosting Memory/Disk Evasion Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Process Ghosting is explicitly named as an evasion method in the title. This technique unmaps a process's memory backing from disk while maintaining execution, evading static analysis and full-disk scanning. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for this Windows-specific technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where the on-disk image is deleted or inaccessible immediately after spawning (file unlink concurrent with process birth or before child module loads). Monitor for CreateRemoteThread + NtSetInformationFile(DELETE) patterns. Flag processes where executable path resolves as deleted.

suggestion.title: Cruciferra Crypter File Signature and Behavioral Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Cruciferra Crypter' as a specific malware tool; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Even without hash indicators in article text, behavioral patterns (crypter-specific PE mutations, obfuscation markers, encryption routines, payload delivery methods) should trigger use-case generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish file signature detections for known Cruciferra samples (via VirusTotal or threat feeds if hashes published). Behavioral detection: monitor for process execution with suspicious file properties (packed/obfuscated sections, entropy spikes), combined with subsequent driver loading or process hollowing attempts.

suggestion.title: Elevation via Vulnerable Driver with Subsequent Privilege Abuse
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD's purpose is privilege escalation; pipeline did not map the chain from driver-load → privilege-elevation → malware-execution. This is the kill-chain core and central to detecting Cruciferra's attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process execution of low-integrity or user-mode process → driver load from same session → child process spawned with elevated token or altered DACL. Look for SYSTEM/TrustedInstaller processes launched from unexpected parents after vulnerable driver load in same session tree.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated File Delivery and Staging Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Crypter tools always involve obfuscation/encryption of payloads. Article emphasizes both BYOVD and Process Ghosting for *hiding*—implying payload staging, encryption, and decryption routines. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for these behavioral indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation with high entropy (packed/encrypted), followed by loading into a parent process's memory, followed by code injection or child execution. Monitor for temporary file staging in user directories with unusual creation/access/delete sequencing (decrypt-in-place pattern).

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API Calls for C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes Telegram is the C2 channel; this is the primary attack delivery mechanism and should be the lead detection. Detect Telegram API endpoints (api.telegram.org) contacted by unexpected processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process-to-Telegram API communication (api.telegram.org, core.telegram.org). Flag processes outside browser/messaging apps initiating HTTPS to Telegram ports (443, 8443) with bot token patterns in TLS SNI or HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: TELESHIM Executable Characteristics
suggestion.rationale: Article names TELESHIM but pipeline extracted no file hashes, names, or process signatures. Malware family should surface associated hashes and executable metadata from threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline TELESHIM samples by hash and code-signing characteristics. Alert on execution of unsigned PE files matching TELESHIM signatures, or on processes spawning with command-line tokens matching Telegram bot patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Telegram Messages
suggestion.rationale: Attacks against government imply data theft; Telegram C2 typically exfiltrates via encrypted messages. Article context ('attacks against Middle East governments') suggests espionage objective but no exfiltration detection surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes writing credential files, registry hives, or documents immediately before initiating Telegram API connections. Flag for high-volume message sends to single Telegram chat ID that correlate with sensitive data access.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Spear Phishing or Watering Hole
suggestion.rationale: Article title does not detail initial compromise vector explicitly in truncated body, but C2-centric attacks require initial infection. Pipeline should have surface techniques even if delivery mechanism unclear from title alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate government-sector email with macro-enabled documents, suspicious links, or weaponized PDFs. Alert on Office process spawning unusual children (cmd, powershell, rundll32) that subsequently contact external C2.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — this is the exploit and should be directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication logs for login tokens issued without preceding successful authentication or from unauthenticated API endpoints. Flag token generation where the originating request lacks valid credentials.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin-Privileged Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow explicitly: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — privilege escalation via token must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect assignment of full admin privileges to SmartConsole tokens that originated unauthenticated or from anomalous sources. Flag admin-level actions performed by tokens created outside normal provisioning workflows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' — standard asset-exposure hunt per template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-16232 matches against SmartConsole instances. Cross-correlate with patch status and federal remediation deadline of 2026-07-25 to identify non-compliant assets.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Internet Exposure Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: KEV status implies 'active exploitation against exposed assets' — internet-facing SmartConsole is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate SmartConsole instances with inbound access from untrusted networks (internet-routable addresses). Flag any externally-accessible SmartConsole running vulnerable versions without WAF/EDR protection.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SmartConsole Administrative Actions Post-Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attack persists via token reuse with 'full administrative privileges' — detect admin actions anomalous to normal baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal SmartConsole admin action patterns. Detect admin-level configuration changes, user provisioning, or policy modifications performed by tokens with suspicious acquisition (unauthenticated origin, non-US geolocation for federal environments).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SmartConsole Admin Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token and use[s] it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' without legitimate credentials — core exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication endpoints for token generation requests lacking standard credential exchange (username/password POST, certificate validation, etc.). Look for token issuance followed immediately by administrative API calls. Baseline legitimate token patterns first; anomalies = exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Exposed SmartConsole Public-Facing Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attacker' and 'public-facing application' — exploitation requires network exposure. Scanning/enumeration of exposed ports is prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Proactively scan for publicly routable SmartConsole services (TCP 443 on typical Check Point ports; banner identifies SmartConsole). Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for unpatched instances. Alert on any new public exposure of SmartConsole.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Authentication Bypass Token
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker gaining 'full administrative privileges' after token theft — privilege escalation without role-based access control enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track token lifecycle: when a token issued from unauthenticated or low-privilege context is used to execute administrative operations (user/group management, policy changes, configuration export). Baseline legitimate admin paths; deviations indicate token hijacking.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Attempt Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Generic exploitation signature for known-exploited CVE — CISA KEV indicates active weaponization; organizations need signature-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS payloads targeting SmartConsole authentication endpoints with patterns known to bypass validation (missing/malformed auth headers, token injection into request parameters, etc.). Correlate with CVE-2026-16232 PoC indicators if available. Flag all attempts regardless of success.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Auth Bypass: Unauthenticated Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' Core exploitation step requires detection on SmartConsole auth service logs for tokens issued without valid credential exchange.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole authentication service for token issuance events where the requesting principal is unauthenticated or lacks credentials. Flag token generation to null/empty identities or rapid-fire token requests from anonymous sources.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Unauthenticated to Admin Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' This is explicit privilege escalation from no auth to admin; must alert on unexpected admin session creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative session creation in SmartConsole originating from unauthenticated or untrusted callers. Alert when a session's privilege level exceeds the authenticated identity's assigned role or when admin grants are issued outside normal workflow.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Check Point SmartConsole Internet-Facing
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires 'remote attacker' network access. KEV active-exploitation context implies public-facing SmartConsole instances; asset inventory must identify these.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory and configurations to identify Check Point SmartConsole instances listening on public-facing IPs or accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with threat intel feeds for active exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Alternate Auth: Stolen Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'obtain an application login token and use it to authenticate.' Attacker uses stolen/obtained token as alternate authentication material for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole API and management interface logs for authentication using tokens that originated from unauthenticated or exploited auth flows. Correlate token creation timestamps with subsequent API calls; alert on token reuse from unexpected geographic IPs.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection: CVE-2026-16232 Attack Traffic
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active wild exploitation. Network and IDS logs should contain exploitation attempts exploiting CVE-2026-16232 improper authentication flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to SmartConsole authentication endpoints with known exploit payloads for CVE-2026-16232 authentication bypass. Flag requests using malformed auth headers, null credentials, or known bypass parameters.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: CVE-2026-16232 Unpatched Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-16232 — match against your vulnerability scanner' with federal patch due 2026-07-25. VulnMgmt systems must flag any unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanning tools for CVE-2026-16232 findings on Check Point SmartConsole. Flag any unpatched systems with exposure older than federal due date as compliance violation and immediate remediation requirement.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Token Issuance to Unauthenticated Clients
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — this is the exploitation vector and must be detectable
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole for API endpoints (/api/login, /auth/token, /api/admin) issuing authentication tokens (Bearer tokens, session cookies, JWT) to requests originating from unauthenticated or external-network sources. Correlate token issuance with absence of prior multi-factor authentication events.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Administrative Privilege Escalation via Stolen Token

Cross-reference source IPs against known-user login geography and timing. Flag any token issuance where auth-step logs are absent or timestamps show auth bypass.

suggestion.title: Kiro Authentication Bypass or Authorization Boundary Violation

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation via Token

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Patterns

Track HTTP/API requests that return valid session tokens without traversing normal login endpoints. Flag 401 → 200 sequences that skip credential submission.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation from Stolen Token

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Exposed Instance Asset Discovery

Alert when admin-level operations originate from sessions with no prior credential validation or marked as low-privilege in auth logs. Identify anomalous privilege assignment patterns where user permissions escalate without explicit promotion events.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Public-Facing Authentication Endpoint Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CVE mapped to T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Article describes remote exploitation: 'unauthenticated remote attacker' accessing authentication endpoints directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole HTTPS endpoints (port 443, /api/auth*, /login, /token) for malformed requests: empty credentials, null auth headers, injection attempts, or serialization payloads. Detect high-volume auth attempts from single sources in short time windows (enumeration). Alert on successful token responses (HTTP 200) to authentication endpoints from external or non-administrative source IPs, especially first-seen IPs.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: T1190 exploitation requires public-facing access. Article implies SmartConsole instances may be exposed: 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' indicates need for asset-exposure validation to confirm proper firewall segmentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Check Point SmartConsole instances via vulnerability scanner or network inventory. Verify each instance's network exposure: cross-reference against firewall ACLs and routing tables to confirm inbound HTTPS (443) is restricted to trusted administrative networks. Alert on any SmartConsole instance reachable from internet or untrusted VLAN. Cross-correlate with patch status from vulnerability scanner to identify unpatched exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Unauthenticated Admin Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token and use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'—token generation from no-auth state is the core exploitation vector and must be detected at source.
log_sources: Check Point SmartConsole REST API logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole login/token endpoints for responses returning valid auth tokens (200 OK, token in response body) when the request lacks valid pre-authentication credentials or authorization headers. Detect rapid or suspicious POST requests to /api/web/login or equivalent returning 200 when 401 would be expected.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Privilege Escalation — Token-Granted Admin Access
suggestion.rationale: Captured token 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'—immediate execution of high-privilege operations after token generation from unauthenticated origin is the attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid admin-privilege exercise (policy changes, user provisioning, export/dump operations) immediately following a token generation event with no prior valid admin session. Flag cases where administrative actions execute within seconds of CVE-2026-16232 exploitation artifacts.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Attempts—SmartConsole Remote Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and 'unauthenticated remote attacker'—need signature/pattern detection for exploitation attempts themselves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests targeting Check Point SmartConsole management ports (443 or configured mgmt port) from external/non-admin network ranges with exploitation patterns: POST requests to authentication endpoints with unusual payloads, requests missing auth headers that return success codes, or multiple failed auth attempts followed immediately by token-generation success.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Once admin token is obtained, attacker gains immediate capability for admin operations: 'use it...with full administrative privileges' implies discovery and lateral-movement queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume or unusual administrative queries immediately after suspected CVE-2026-16232 exploitation: user/object enumeration calls, policy export attempts, permission queries, or configuration dumps initiated from newly-created admin sessions that lack prior legitimate admin activity history.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Network Exposure (CISA KEV Asset Inventory)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Check Point SmartConsole management interfaces and verify they are NOT reachable from untrusted networks (internet, guest VLANs, non-admin segments). Audit firewall ACLs permitting inbound HTTPS on SmartConsole ports (443 default) from external CIDR ranges. Enforce admin VPN-only access.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Token Acquisition via SmartConsole Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — this is the core exploit step and requires detection of token issuance without corresponding login/authentication events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication logs for authorization tokens issued to external/untrusted source IPs without corresponding credential submission or successful login. Correlate token timestamps against session initiation logs.

suggestion.title: Admin API Access via Exploited Authentication Token
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows attacker to 'authenticate with full administrative privileges' using obtained token — detect administrative actions executed through tokens acquired via CVE-2026-16232 exploit path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag administrative API calls to SmartConsole (user creation, policy modification, role assignment) from token-authenticated sessions lacking session context or initiated from external networks. Alert on admin actions from tokens with abnormally short lifetime.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Presence in Inventory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory check for Check Point SmartConsole installations and version matching against known-vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-16232. Flag unpatched systems exposed to network with due-date reminders for July 2026 federal mandate.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing SmartConsole Exploitation Probe Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' — detect reconnaissance and exploitation attempts targeting exposed SmartConsole admin interfaces and auth endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/S traffic to SmartConsole authentication and administrative URIs from external source IPs. suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation from Token Misuse
suggestion.rationale: Exploit grants 'full administrative privileges' via token — detect lateral movement and privilege escalation within SmartConsole following token acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag role elevation, permission grants, or security group membership changes in SmartConsole when originating from non-privileged tokens or external authentication sources. Monitor for first-time admin actions from previously non-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Acquisition

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Admin API Access Without Prior Auth Event

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Issuance Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Attempts Against SmartConsole

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unusual Remote Admin Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated remote attacker gaining admin token enables lateral movement and persistence. Post-compromise activity needs baselining.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Issuance Detected

Cross-reference token issuance with authentication log—alert if token appears in access logs without a corresponding successful login.

suggestion.title: Administrative Actions from Unauthenticated Session Token

Alert if admin actions trace back to tokens flagged as unauthenticated or malformed in auth logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Attempts to Public SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'exploit public-facing application' and CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild—network detection is needed.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SmartConsole Authentication Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token' without authentication. Detect tokens issued to unauthenticated or failed-auth sessions.

suggestion.title: Privileged Admin Operations via Suspicious/New Authentication Tokens

Alert when admin operations occur from tokens without prior login events, from unexpected source IPs, or from tokens with unusually short generation-to-use intervals. suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Check Point SmartConsole Asset Inventory

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'improper authentication.' Detect requests that succeed despite missing or malformed auth credentials.

Track requests that omit standard auth fields yet receive privileged data. Correlate against known Check Point auth-bypass CVE patterns.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole API Token Claims Validation Failure
suggestion.rationale: Attack uses obtained token to impersonate admin. Detect tokens where embedded claims (privileges/roles) diverge from baseline for that user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode SmartConsole auth tokens (JWT or equivalent) in API logs and validate embedded role claims. Alert when tokens claim admin role for users with no prior admin access, or when privilege level in token exceeds user's baseline permissions.

suggestion.title: Rapid SmartConsole Policy and User Changes Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains admin token, malicious configuration changes typically follow. Detect policy/user modification clusters post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline SmartConsole change frequency per admin. Alert on sudden clusters of policy edits, user additions, rule modifications, or logging-config disables within 30 minutes of a detected auth anomaly or suspicious token generation.

suggestion.title: Orphaned commit creation in production GitHub repos
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes orphaned commits as key enabling factor: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch.' This defensive tactic hides attack code from routine branch reviews.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits reachable via direct hash or tag reference but unreachable from any live branch. Alert when orphaned commits appear in critical repos, especially if followed by tag reassignments. Correlate against expected development workflows.

suggestion.title: Release tag reassignment or retroactive repointing
suggestion.rationale: Core obfuscation: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'changing existing release tags to point to the attack commit.' Developers expect immutable tag-to-commit bindings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag tag creation/deletion/update events on repositories with >1k external dependents (found via GitHub dependency graph). Alert if semantic version tag (e.g., v35) is deleted then recreated pointing to a different commit within days. Cross-check against release notes.

suggestion.title: Secrets leaked in plaintext within GitHub Actions logs
suggestion.rationale: Direct impact vector: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Article implies normal GitHub encryption was bypassed or misconfigured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse GitHub Actions run logs (public or archived) for plaintext AWS keys, API tokens, DB passwords, or private URLs. Regex entropy detection for secrets. Flag if repo has >50 external stargazers (public visibility increases risk). Correlate with recent workflow modifications or dependency updates.

suggestion.title: External network calls from GitHub Actions workflows
suggestion.rationale: Attack detection vector: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted external domains. Alert on first-seen domains or IPs contacted from Actions workflows. Correlate with recent Action modifications or inherited dependencies. Flag connections to known C2 infrastructure or newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized repository write access or permission grant

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new write-level collaborators added to high-dependency repos (filter by external dependents via API). Flag if permission granted by low-activity or newly-created accounts. Correlate with failed login attempts in preceding hours. Require approval for write-level grants on repos with >500 stars.

suggestion.title: Discovery and mapping of public GitHub Actions dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Attacker targeted a repo relied upon by 23k other repos. Suggests reconnaissance of popular Actions via GitHub API, dependency graphs, or security advisories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk API queries to GitHub's dependency endpoints (repos/X/dependents endpoint or dependency-graph endpoints). Alert if attacker enumeration profiles repositories by star-count, fork-count, or depends-on relationships. Baseline API usage per threat actor or IP.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole: Unauthenticated Admin Token Generation

suggestion.title: SmartConsole: Public-Facing Authentication Bypass Exploitation

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Administrative Privilege Escalation via Token
suggestion.rationale: Article states acquired token grants 'full administrative privileges'—this is privilege escalation. Pipeline kill chain should have mapped this but is empty.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect tokens with admin claims used for operations (configuration changes, user management). Alert on privilege elevation from non-admin contexts or tokens issued to unprivileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Check Point SmartConsole Network Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes publicly-facing application exploitation risk. Article mentions 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure' but pipeline generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed Check Point SmartConsole ports (default 443, 8080 for web console) reachable from non-trusted networks. Cross-reference with patch status to identify unpatched instances exposed post-CVE publication date.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes improper auth allowing bypass. Pipeline should generate detection for exploitation attempts (malformed auth requests, token manipulation). Not present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to SmartConsole authentication endpoints missing credentials or containing malformed auth headers. Flag requests attempting to bypass authentication checks or directly accessing token endpoints.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — this is the core attack vector and must be detected at token generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when SmartConsole generates a valid authentication token in response to a request without valid credentials. Monitor for /login or /api/auth endpoints returning 200 status + token to requests that fail credential validation. Baseline legitimate token generation and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Action from New/Anomalous Token
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'use[s] it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — detectable via correlating token creation time with subsequent admin operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative configuration changes, policy pushes, or user account modifications in SmartConsole where the authenticated user token was created within the last 60 minutes and source IP is external, recently-seen, or non-whitelisted.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole External Exposure
suggestion.rationale: T1190 requires public-facing application; article indicates active exploitation — must identify externally-accessible SmartConsole instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for SmartConsole HTTPS listeners (ports 4434, 4435) accessible from internet-routable IPs. Cross-reference with internal inventory to identify shadow instances or misconfigured firewall rules. Prioritize based on CISA KEV urgency (patch due 2026-07-25).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Signature
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active exploitation in the wild; PoC likely circulating — need IDS/WAF signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Check threat intel feeds (Shodan, CVE advisories, exploit DBs) for known CVE-2026-16232 exploitation signatures. Flag HTTP requests with documented bypass payloads, malformed auth headers, or API endpoint manipulation patterns documented in proof-of-concept code.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Public-Facing Service Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' and an 'unauthenticated remote attacker' scenario, implying internet-exposed SmartConsole instances. No use case generated to hunt these.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SmartConsole listeners (typical ports 18211 or 18190) visible on public IPs or accessible from external networks. Correlate with CVE-2026-16232 patch status via vulnerability scanner. Flag any organization with unpatched, internet-facing SmartConsole.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' Pipeline missed this credential-access step entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication logs for token issuance events (login_token, session_token) that lack a corresponding successful authentication or that occur from contexts marked unauthenticated. Baseline normal token generation patterns; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Privilege Escalation via Stolen Token
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain continues: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' No use case to detect admin actions immediately following token compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within SmartConsole, detect admin-level actions (policy changes, user creation, object deletion) performed by a newly-authenticated session shortly after an anomalous token generation event. Correlate privilege level at token time vs. privilege level at action time.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Token Reuse Across Session Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Attacker reuses the stolen token in a different context (unauthenticated session → authenticated admin session). No use case to detect this context-crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track SmartConsole authentication tokens and their usage context (source IP, User-Agent, session start time). Alert if a single token is used across multiple IP addresses, user agents, or session IDs within a short time window—signature of token theft and reuse.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole CVE-2026-16232 Scanner-to-Telemetry Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-16232 with patch due 2026-07-25. Standard practice: correlate unpatched assets from vuln scanners with observed exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract list of assets vulnerable to CVE-2026-16232 from scanner. Cross-reference with inbound web logs and IDS alerts targeting SmartConsole. Flag any connection attempts to unpatched SmartConsole instances post-CVE publication (2026-07-22).

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'obtain an application login token' without authentication credentials. This is the exploitation mechanism and must be detected by monitoring abnormal token generation events in SmartConsole logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SmartConsole authentication token issuance without preceding successful login event or MFA challenge. Scope to tokens with admin claims or API scope. Alert within 60 seconds of external connection to TCP/443 or 4434 (Check Point SmartConsole ports) lacking valid credential submission.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation via Token
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies obtained token grants 'full administrative privileges' immediately. Detect privilege boundary violations when token from external source performs admin operations (configuration changes, account creation, policy modifications).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SmartConsole sessions that execute administrative API calls (e.g., add_administrator, set_policy) within first 3 minutes of token acquisition, especially from external/non-managed IPs. Correlate token lifecycle events with policy or object modifications.

suggestion.title: External Network Access to SmartConsole Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote attacker' accessing SmartConsole—vulnerability is network-exposed. Baseline allowed external access and detect exploitation attempts from unauthorized IP space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish whitelist of known-good external IP ranges (VPN, partner, security team) accessing SmartConsole admin interface. Alert on login attempts to /admin, /api/login, or /app/login from non-whitelisted external IPs. Increase sensitivity for versions matching CVE-2026-16232 detection signatures.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Patch Bypass: Unpatched Despite Scanner Reports
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check'—suggests patch evasion or scanner deception. Detect systems claiming patched that exhibit exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CMDB records showing CVE-2026-16232 patched (version ≥ known-safe build) with SmartConsole authentication anomalies, token generation, or admin operations. Flag as patch bypass or evasion; escalate for manual patch verification.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — core attack vector requiring immediate detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole token generation APIs for requests without prior authentication events. Look for token_grant or session_create calls with source IP/account lacking valid authentication record in preceding seconds.

suggestion.title: Privileged Admin Operations via Unauthenticated-Origin Token
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attackers 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — detecting admin actions from compromised tokens is critical to containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate token acquisition events (no auth) with subsequent admin-level operations (policy modification, account creation, config changes). Flag admin actions where token provenance is unauthenticated-acquired.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing SmartConsole Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: KEV status confirms 'active exploitation against exposed assets' — externally-accessible SmartConsole instances are immediately under attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory: flag SmartConsole instances on routable public IPs. Correlate external inbound traffic to SmartConsole ports with authentication-bypass attempts in application logs. Alert on unauthenticated API calls from internet-sourced IPs.

suggestion.title: Token-Based Administrative Access Without Interactive Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Attack bypasses normal auth flow entirely — legitimate admins authenticate interactively first; attackers obtain token directly. This behavioral gap is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal admin patterns (interactive login → admin session). Alert on admin operations that skip interactive authentication phase (programmatic token → privileged API calls within seconds). Monitor for token reuse across multiple admin-level changes.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Internet-Facing Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker' can exploit—explicit network reachability requirement. Baseline asset inventory required to scope blast radius.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network segmentation and vulnerability scanner for Check Point SmartConsole instances accessible from untrusted networks (DMZ, internet). Correlate with CVE-2026-16232 detection. Flag any exposed instances for emergency patching.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Admin Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain...login token...full administrative privileges.' Token issuance without prior valid authentication is the exploitation event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when SmartConsole issues admin authentication tokens to sessions showing no prior successful user login, no valid auth headers, or suspicious timing/source. Focus on token creation events from unexpected IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Admin Actions via SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Stolen admin tokens enable unauthorized actions. Article implies full admin capability—persistence, lateral movement, or policy manipulation likely follow exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for admin-level policy changes, credential resets, rule disables, or user provisioning from non-whitelisted IP addresses or at times inconsistent with normal admin windows. Prioritize changes that weaken security posture (firewall disables, bypass rules).

suggestion.title: Admin Token Reuse from Anomalous Locations
suggestion.rationale: Tokens issued to attacker will be used from attacker infrastructure, not legitimate admin workstations. Behavioral anomaly signals exploitation success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin tokens used simultaneously or in rapid succession from disparate geographic locations. Correlate token session IDs with source IP geolocation and compare to historical admin behavior. Flag impossible-travel scenarios.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole API Abuse by Compromised Token
suggestion.rationale: Admin tokens can invoke SmartConsole API for infrastructure-wide changes. Bulk operations or unusual API calls using stolen tokens indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls made with admin-context tokens for mass-policy deployments, credential resets, object deletions, or reconnaissance queries (system inventory enumeration). Alert on API calls from non-standard client User-Agents or SDK versions.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Unauthenticated Auth Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token'. Attack surface is the auth endpoint itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to SmartConsole auth paths (typically /api/auth, /login) from untrusted sources returning 200–302 without credentials, or issuing auth tokens to anonymous sessions. SmartConsole default ports: 4434 (HTTPS), 443.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Privilege Escalation via Stolen Auth Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'. Implies token theft followed by admin-level actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag auth tokens issued to anomalous contexts (new IP, off-hours, failed login immediately prior) that perform admin actions (policy write, account creation, config export) within minutes of issuance. Token lifecycle correlation is key.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Network Exposure (CVE-2026-16232)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker'. Standard asset-exposure hunt for internet-facing or untrusted-network-accessible SmartConsole instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory SmartConsole instances listening on ports 4434 or 443 from internet or untrusted segments. Cross-ref patch status against vendor advisory; any unpatched build is exploitable. Federal due date passed 2026-07-25.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin-Level API Activity from Stolen Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'full administrative privileges' after token theft. Lateral movement / privilege abuse use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole API calls (e.g., via /api/mgmt endpoints) for admin-gated operations (policy updates, user provisioning, gateway config changes) initiated by sessions lacking normal login audit trail. Correlate with external network access or off-hours activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Remediation Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-16232 as CISA KEV (active exploitation observed). Compliance check: patch status across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Check Point SmartConsole versions ≤ [vendor-specified build]. Cross-check with installed patches. CISA KEV entries carry mandatory federal remediation deadlines; non-compliance is auditable. Alert on any unpatched instance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Token Generation in SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states attacker can 'obtain an application login token' without authentication. This is the root exploit — detect tokens issued to requests with no valid credential chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole /api/login and /api/auth endpoints for tokens issued without corresponding authentication events (MFA, username/password validation, or API key exchange). Successful token generation to unauthenticated sessions is anomalous; baseline token issuance rate and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: Administrative Privilege Escalation via Stolen Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes token grants attacker 'full administrative privileges.' Admin API calls using newly-minted tokens bypass normal authorization chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin-level API calls (policy modifications, user provisioning, gateway config export) executed by tokens lacking standard authentication path metadata. Flag tokens used for privilege-level operations that exceed the token's claimed identity.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote attacker' — this is T1190 exploitation against exposed management interface. Detect scanning and exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to SmartConsole auth endpoints from external IPs with missing/malformed Authorization headers or known exploit payload signatures. Correlate failed auth attempts with successful token generation to identify successful exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog guidance requires asset-exposure hunts — scanner must match CVE-2026-16232 against Check Point inventory to identify unpatched internet-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner CVE-2026-16232 matches against Check Point SmartConsole inventory. Even if patches reported, verify version compliance and confirm no unpatched SmartConsole 2024.x or earlier are externally reachable.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Admin Activity via Compromised Tokens
suggestion.rationale: After token theft ('obtain...login token'), attacker uses it to execute admin commands. Hunt for unusual admin activity from token-based sessions.
log_sources: Check Point SmartConsole command audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify administrative commands (create/modify users, policy pushes, configuration exports) executed by tokens without associated session context (VPN, MFA, identity binding). Flag activity within 5 minutes of token issuance to external source.

suggestion.title: Blockchain-based C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Blockchain C2'—a fundamental shift from traditional IP/domain-based C2. No use case was generated for this novel infrastructure despite it being the headline innovation described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IoT and edge devices establishing sustained connections to Ethereum/Bitcoin RPC endpoints or blockchain API gateways with high-frequency command-like traffic patterns. Monitor for crypto library instantiation (web3.py, ethers.js) on systems not expected to interact with blockchains.

suggestion.title: IoT Peer-to-Peer Relay Node Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Victim Relays' as post-disruption resilience mechanism. This describes compromised IoT devices forwarding botnet traffic to evade centralized C2 takedown—critical persistence and distribution technique absent from UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag IoT/edge devices exhibiting atypical relay behavior: high-volume peer-to-peer connections, forwarding traffic between internal networks and external nodes, or acting as bridges with minimal direct outbound communication. Track connection symmetry anomalies (many inbound, few outbound).

suggestion.title: Dysphoria Malware Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Dysphoria is named explicitly in the title as the botnet family, yet pipeline extracted zero malware signatures, file hashes, process names, or behavioral IoCs. Malware-family-specific detections are foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Dysphoria malware process artifacts (known hash signatures, embedded configuration strings, registry persistence paths). Detect spawned child processes attempting network socket setup for P2P relay participation or blockchain query tools.

suggestion.title: Post-Disruption IoT Device Re-infection
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'After JackSkid Disruption'—indicating this is a resurgence campaign. Initial access mechanism (credential compromise, exploitation) must be detected to block re-infection. No baseline provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IoT management ports (SSH:22, HTTP:80, HTTPS:443, Telnet:23) for brute-force attempts and exploitation payloads targeting known IoT vulnerabilities. Alert on successful credential use from untrusted sources followed by suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Wallet Cluster Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Botnets monetize via DDoS-as-a-service; blockchain integration implies wallet addresses for payment collection. No wallet IOCs or blockchain transaction patterns were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track publicly known Dysphoria botnet wallet addresses on blockchain explorers. Correlate internal hosts querying blockchain APIs for wallet balance checks or transaction confirmation patterns. Flag organizations whose compromised IoT subnets generate blockchain transactions.

suggestion.title: Machine Account Creation by Low-Privileged Users
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'a low-privileged user first creates a machine account, which is permitted under the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota configuration.' This is the attack's initial stepping stone that should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on machine account creation (event 4741) by non-service principals. Filter for accounts below helpdesk/sysadmin groups. Baseline ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota usage and flag when quota reached or multiple accounts created by single low-priv user in short window.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Certificate Authority Network Connections to Non-DC Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'the CA connects to the server specified in the cdc value and searches for the specified rmd'—the attack redirects CA to attacker-controlled SMB/LSA/LDAP. CA→non-DC endpoints are rare.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CA server (certutil, CertSrv processes) initiating outbound SMB (445), LDAP (389,636), or LSA (49152+) connections to non-whitelisted domain controller IPs. Flag connections to workstation or non-DC server IPs from CA service account.

suggestion.title: PKINIT Authentication as Domain Controller
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using the certificate to authenticate through PKINIT as the targeted domain controller.' Kerberos AS-REQ with DC computer account using certificate-based auth is anomalous and precedes DCSync.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Kerberos AS-REQ (4768) where client is a Domain Controller computer account and authentication method is certificate-based (PKINIT). Cross-correlate with immediate subsequent TGS requests for directory replication rights.

suggestion.title: DCSync Activity from Non-Replication Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates: 'With the resulting Kerberos credential, the attacker can request account secrets, including the krbtgt secret.' DCSync from an unexpected account principal should trigger immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GetNCChanges RPC calls (event 4662, ObjectClass=domainDNS, replication rights check) initiated by non-replication-service principals. Flag any requester attempting replication for krbtgt account or multiple sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Certificate Enrollment Requests Targeting Domain Controller Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Certighost: 'submit a certificate request that directs the CA to the rogue services and targets a domain controller account.' Cert requests for DC accounts are highly anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag certificate enrollment requests where subject CN is a Domain Controller computer account (name$) submitted by non-admin/certificate-requester account. Monitor for requests with unusual cdc or rmd attributes (if CA logs these).

suggestion.title: Kerberos Credentials Saved to Disk (.ccache files)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes PoC 'saving the resulting Kerberos credentials to a .ccache file.' Presence of .ccache files outside expected tool directories signals credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .ccache file creation outside /tmp and standard Kerberos paths. Flag if created by non-kerberos processes or in user home directories. Correlate with preceding certificate enrollment and PKINIT activity.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Pre-Auth RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Public Exploit Released for Patched vBulletin Pre-Auth Code Execution Flaw'—establishes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Pipeline must detect HTTP requests to vBulletin admin/api endpoints with known exploit payloads or suspicious parameter values characteristic of RCE attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for HTTP POST requests to vBulletin endpoints (e.g., /admincp/, /ajax.php, /api/) containing known exploit signatures or unexpected serialized PHP objects. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses followed by unusual process execution from web service accounts.

suggestion.title: Web-to-Process RCE Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: A pre-auth code execution flaw implies unauthenticated attackers gain arbitrary command execution. Article title confirms this attack vector; detection should cover process spawning from web server contexts (apache/www-data/iis apppool).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from vBulletin web service accounts with suspicious parent process patterns. Flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell interpreters invoked by w3wp.exe, httpd, or apache with encoded arguments or suspicious LOLBins.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Web Shell Upload or File Staging
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of public RCE often leads to persistence via web shells. Article context implies potential for follow-on file writes to web-accessible directories post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new .php, .asp, .aspx, .jsp files created in vBulletin directories (includes/, upload/, cache/) within minutes of exploitation attempt logs. Correlate file creation with anomalous HTTP POST requests or web server process spawning child interpreters.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Vulnerable Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit disclosure typically targets specific patched versions. Detection must identify unpatched vBulletin instances via version headers, install paths, or /admincp/ responses that leak version info.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse HTTP response headers and error pages from vBulletin endpoints for version strings (e.g., 'vBulletin 5.6.x' in Server header or page source). Flag instances running versions known to be vulnerable to this RCE flaw based on CVE timeline.

suggestion.title: vBulletin C2 Callback Detection Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation enables reverse shells or data exfiltration. Article's critical severity and public exploit suggest rapid weaponization; detection must cover outbound network activity from compromised vBulletin servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from vBulletin server IPs to high-risk TLDs or known C2 infrastructure. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains resolved by web service accounts or child processes of vBulletin.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Data Exfiltration (Forum/User Database)
suggestion.rationale: RCE against forum software typically leads to database theft. Article context implies attacker can read database.php or execute queries; detection should cover bulk data reads or export patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large SELECT queries against vBulletin database (vbulletin.user table) or unexpected database table exports. Correlate with outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from vBulletin server carrying structured data (serialized PHP, JSON with user credentials).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits via 'crafted HTTP requests' against FortiOS. No use case generated despite CISA KEV status (active exploitation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to FortiOS management interfaces with abnormal headers, payloads, or response codes. Correlate with known-bad user agents and POST patterns matching CVE-2025-68686 proof-of-concept signatures. Focus on unauthenticated requests given 'remote unauthenticated attacker' capability.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as attack vector. Pipeline ignored filesystem-level persistence indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS application directories for symlink creation via `ln -s` or Windows equivalents post-compromise. Baseline FortiOS filesystem structure and alert on modifications to `/etc/`, `/var/`, or application startup paths containing symbolic references.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Verification vs. CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch bypass and federal due-date 2026-08-10. Pipeline did not generate compliance/asset-exposure use case despite CISA requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Fortinet FortiOS instances and compare running versions against patched versions post-2026-08-10. Alert on any instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 even if patch claims exist—verify actual deployment via process enumeration or file hashes.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Traffic to FortiOS Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Attack path explicitly requires 'crafted HTTP requests' but no traffic pattern detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP request morphology: oversized headers, null-byte injection, malformed Content-Length, or request methods (TRACE, OPTIONS) to admin endpoints. Flag requests with exploit payload signatures (base64 binary, serialized objects, format strings) in URI or POST body.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Patch Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Implies active anti-forensic or evasion post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion or modification of FortiOS security module files, patches, or logging directories after T1190 detection. Flag attempts to re-link or restore vulnerable symlinks post-patch. Monitor for file attribute changes (chmod 000, immutable flag removal) on security-critical paths.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure Post-CVE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes vulnerability 'may allow...exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' but no data-exfiltration or collection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiOS HTTP egress traffic size and patterns. Alert on anomalous data volume from FortiOS management interfaces post-CVE-2025-68686 exploitation window. Flag DNS queries or HTTP requests to attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoints from FortiOS network context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable FortiOS Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes CVE-2025-68686 as 'observed exploited in the wild' CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-08-10; vulnerability scan results must surface unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiOS instances reporting CVE-2025-68686 as vulnerable or unpatched. Prioritize those exposed to public internet. Flag any systems past the 2026-08-10 federal patch deadline without remediation.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Against FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'remote unauthenticated attacker' sending 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patches; requires detection of malicious HTTP patterns against FortiOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor public-facing FortiOS instances for unusual HTTP request patterns: abnormal method/header combinations, path traversal attempts, polyglot payloads, or request sequences that match known CVE-2025-68686 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Filesystem-Compromise Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' then exploits via HTTP; chain detection needed for two-stage attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for prior filesystem-level compromise indicators on FortiOS (unauthorized file writes, symlink creation, privilege escalation attempts). Correlate with subsequent HTTP exploitation attempts to catch the complete attack chain.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—requires detection of unauthorized access to config, credentials, or encryption material post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS configuration file access, credential API calls, and encryption key operations following successful HTTP exploitation. Flag abnormal egress traffic carrying configuration or credential data.

suggestion.title: Public Internet Exposure of FortiOS Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' as prerequisite for unauthenticated remote exploitation; requires pre-exploitation asset discovery hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference external internet-facing scan results (Censys, Shodan equivalents) against internal asset inventory. Identify and alert on FortiOS appliances accessible from the internet, prioritizing those matching CVE-2025-68686 vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Administrative Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker...via crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated no detection logic for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin interfaces for unusual HTTP request patterns, malformed headers, or suspicious parameter combinations. Baseline legitimate admin traffic and alert on requests matching known CVE-2025-68686 exploit signatures or polyglot payloads attempting authentication bypass.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Traversal on Compromised FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'post-exploit cases,' indicating attackers leverage symlinks for persistence. No persistence-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or traversal of symbolic links in FortiOS system directories (especially config, log, and data paths). Correlate with prior CVE compromises or unusual filesystem access patterns indicating post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access and Exposure on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article core outcome is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline missed data-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk or sequential access to sensitive configuration (VPN credentials, admin accounts, encryption keys, policy definitions) following successful HTTP exploitation. Flag export or copy operations on sensitive files by non-service accounts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure and Patch Coverage Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Standard vulnerability hunting: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and CISA KEV imply active scanning requirement. Pipeline provided template reference but no actual detection scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate all externally accessible FortiOS instances against CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Prioritize assets still running vulnerable versions; cross-reference with threat intel on active exploitation. Include network-accessible management interfaces, SSL VPN gateways, and SD-WAN controllers.

suggestion.title: Bypass of Symbolic Link Persistency Patch (CVE-2025-68686 Specific)

suggestion.title: Symlink Abuse Detection on FortiOS File Systems

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Inventory Drift for Fortinet FortiOS

suggestion.title: Public-only token used to modify private repository resources

Flag when same token with public-only restriction performs write operations on resources marked private, indicating authorization bypass.

suggestion.title: Repository context mismatch in PR update API calls

Detection should flag API calls where the route parameter repo differs from the target resource's actual repo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea API logs for PR update requests where the {public-repo} in the URL path differs from the PR's actual base repository. Mismatch indicates potential authorization context confusion attack.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized branch modifications in private pull requests

After bypass succeeds, detect the actual destructive action—unexpected branch ref changes in private repos via API tokens with limited scope. Article describes the attack outcome but pipeline did not generate impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea repository branch logs for unexpected head branch updates in private repos. Flag when branch refs change via API token activity (not direct commits), especially when the token's scope is public-only or narrower than the target repository's privacy level.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scan

Baseline normal FortiOS traffic patterns and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access from FortiOS Post-Exploitation

Flag reads from filesystem paths normally accessed only by root/system. Correlate data access with prior symlink-creation timelines.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem-Level Compromise Indicators

suggestion.title: Unauthorized or Suspicious Commits to Critical GitHub Action Repositories

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Action Version Tag Drift from Expected Commits
suggestion.rationale: Attack leveraged consumers expecting stable versions: users 'reference that tag and assume that's what we'll be getting. Under normal circumstances, that is a reasonable assumption but GitHub tags are just convenient strings pointing to a particular commit - no magic.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Action tags in workflows against their current commits. Alert when tags deviate from historical commit authors, lack code signatures, or point to commits created outside normal release windows or review processes.

suggestion.title: Gitea artifact access with mismatched task owner context in audit logs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker...can turn a signed URL for an attacker-controlled artifact into a URL that reads artifacts from another task context.' Pipeline missed log-level validation: Gitea audit logs should record artifact operations where the requester's task context does not own/match the target artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DownloadArtifact or UploadArtifact API calls where RequestorJobID ≠ ArtifactOwnerJobID, especially across repositories. Legitimate artifact access is owner-scoped; cross-context access is exploitation.

suggestion.title: Rapid multi-artifact enumeration post-workflow dispatch

Behavioral gap: exploitation would manifest as rapid sequential artifact downloads of varying artifactName values immediately after workflow start—scanning behavior distinct from legitimate workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 30s–2min post-workflow-dispatch, flag 5+ DownloadArtifact requests to distinct artifactName values from single source/job. Normal workflows fetch 1–2 known artifacts; enumeration attempts show randomization or path traversal patterns.

suggestion.title: HMAC signature parameter reuse across repository boundaries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can be rewritten to access a different running task and repository context while preserving the original HMAC signature.' suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract sig parameter from UploadArtifact/DownloadArtifact URLs and correlate across repository names. Alert on same sig accessing 2+ distinct repositories in 10min window—indicates HMAC reuse exploitation across contexts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized writes to artifact staging areas from non-owner task processes

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor artifact upload directories for file writes from gitea-actions runner processes assigned to a different TaskID than the artifact's owner. Mismatch indicates cross-task write exploitation.

suggestion.title: Credential/secret material discovery via cross-task artifact content inspection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'artifacts' without specifying content; but cross-task read attacks gain access to other jobs' build outputs, which often contain secrets, tokens, private keys. Detection: after cross-task artifact read is confirmed, correlate with sensitive patterns in artifact payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enrich cross-task artifact download detections with artifact content analysis: flag high-risk if downloaded artifacts contain regex patterns matching CI_TOKEN=, GITHUB_TOKEN=, AWS_ACCESS_KEY, RSA PRIVATE KEY, etc. Indicates credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiOS Admin Interfaces

Baseline normal admin traffic and alert on deviations, particularly POST/PUT requests with encoded payloads or requests to undocumented endpoints. Correlate with known-exploited CVE-2025-68686 patches.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation/Modification on FortiOS Filesystem

Alert if symbolic link activity resumes post-patch.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage Exploitation: Detect Predecessor Vulnerability Leading to FortiOS Compromise
