suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines for FortiOS data access patterns and egress volumes. Alert on spike in file reads from sensitive paths (credentials, vpn-config, license-keys) or unusual egress connections from appliances carrying extracted data over unencrypted channels.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass via Obfuscated HTTP Payloads to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism via crafted HTTP requests'—indicating polymorphic/encoded exploitation after patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create anomaly rules for HTTP requests attempting to encode or nest path traversal sequences in non-standard locations (cookies, content-encoding, X-Forwarded-* headers, etc.). Monitor for requests that violate expected URL-structure patterns post-patch date (2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Remote Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the core attack vector and warrants detection of anomalous HTTP patterns to FortiOS instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin/API endpoints for crafted payloads characteristic of CVE-2025-68686. Focus on unauthenticated access attempts and unusual parameter combinations that could trigger the integer overflow or bypass logic.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Indicates filesystem-level persistence technique that should be hunted after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for symbolic link creation events on FortiOS systems post-exploitation, particularly in web-accessible directories or configuration paths. Look for file operations that create links to sensitive binaries or config files.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerable Version Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and emphasizes patch lag risk. Need inventory of FortiOS versions and validation that patches are applied before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Fortinet FortiOS instances and map to vulnerable versions (pre-patch cutoff). Cross-reference against patch deployment records to identify systems with delayed or missing patches. Alert on systems still running vulnerable versions post-2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner & Product Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Standard indicator matching against known exploited vulnerability CVE ID and Fortinet FortiOS product signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2025-68686 against asset inventory. Flag any confirmed vulnerable Fortinet FortiOS instances for immediate patching priority, particularly those exposed to internet or untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Filesystem Access After Fortinet Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Indicates multi-stage attack with filesystem-level access as prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After FortiOS compromise via CVE-2025-68686, hunt for suspicious filesystem modifications in sensitive directories (/bin, /lib, /etc). Look for new symlinks, file permission changes, or binary replacements that could establish persistence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL... Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. This is the baseline detection for a CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiOS instances in scope via vulnerability scanner. Cross-reference build version against Fortinet vendor patches for CVE-2025-68686. Flag unpatched instances, prioritizing internet-facing or edge appliances. Match against netflow/firewall logs for external source access to flagged systems.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic-Link Persistency Post-Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'. This is a key persistence indicator requiring filesystem telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system directories and application paths for symbolic link creation or modification by non-standard accounts. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or HTTP anomalies. Inspect symlink targets for escaping confined directories or pointing to sensitive configuration stores.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation vector: 'remote unauthenticated attacker... via crafted HTTP requests'. HTTP request patterns are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP traffic to FortiOS admin interfaces. Flag requests with anomalous payloads: oversized parameters, URL-encoded special characters, null bytes, or repeating sequences. Look for request pattern escalation—multiple malformed requests followed by legitimate access.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Disclosure Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies end-state: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'. This is the data exfiltration phase requiring data-access telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unauthorized read access to credential stores, policy databases, or configuration files. Flag large or suspicious data transfers (compression, encryption, unusual protocols) from compromised instances. Correlate with external C2 communications.

suggestion.title: Federal FortiOS Patch Compliance Tracking (Due 2026-08-10)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and article notes state 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Compliance is operational risk mitigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system for all Fortinet FortiOS systems and their build versions. Compare against Fortinet CVE-2025-68686 fix advisory to identify unpatched systems. Generate risk report by asset criticality. Escalate any unpatched internet-facing systems as P1 for immediate patching prior to 2026-08-10 Federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Detect crafted HTTP requests to FortiOS public interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliances for malformed or anomalously-crafted HTTP requests targeting sensitive endpoints. Look for request patterns that differ from baseline traffic—unusual headers, parameter combinations, or serialization artifacts consistent with CVE-2025-68686 proof-of-concepts once disclosed.

suggestion.title: Detect symbolic link creation on FortiOS filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—adversary establishes persistence after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of symbolic links in FortiOS configuration, startup, or persistence directories (/etc/init.d, /lib/systemd, firmware boot paths). Correlate with prior exploitation attempts to identify post-compromise persistence.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthorized sensitive data access from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—pipeline must detect the exfiltration or unauthorized read of configuration, credentials, or logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unusual file reads targeting sensitive paths (certificates, keys, config files, system logs). Correlate file access events with prior CVE-2025-68686 exploitation signatures and anomalous network egress of config-sized data blobs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 asset exposure hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV inclusion means 'currently being exploited' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with this CVE substituted into the template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiOS instances across your estate using vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable). Flag any systems reporting as vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686, even if patches are claimed applied—verify against FortiOS advisory for exact patch version. Federal due date 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Detect bypass of FortiOS patch via repeated exploitation attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—detection should trigger on repeated or evolved exploitation payloads against patched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track HTTP requests to FortiOS that match exploit signatures but arrive *after* patch deployment. Flag as potential bypass attempts, variant payloads, or zero-day adjacent exploitation. Correlate with vulnerability scanner status to confirm patch was supposedly applied.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the exploitation vector: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the primary detectable attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS administrative interfaces for HTTP requests with atypical parameter sequences, encoding chains, or path-traversal patterns targeting symbolic-link persistency paths. Correlate POST-request sequences with upstream compromise indicators (failed logins, configuration access). Alert on requests attempting to re-trigger the symbolic-link vulnerability after patch deployment.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Extraction from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Core impact stated as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Article specifies prerequisite: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—indicating post-compromise data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detected/suspected FortiOS compromise, monitor for non-routine access to configuration files, credential stores, VPN key material, and admin token repositories. Flag reads from sensitive system paths by unprivileged accounts or from unusual source IPs within 24h post-compromise date.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Patch Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as ability to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' File-system monitoring can detect re-exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of symbolic links in FortiOS application or configuration directories following patch deployment. Correlate symlink creation timing with HTTP request patterns and filesystem access logs to identify re-exploitation of the persistency mechanism.

suggestion.title: Credential Material Exfiltration Post-FortiOS Breach
suggestion.rationale: 'Sensitive information exposure' in VPN/firewall appliance context typically includes authentication credentials, session tokens, and pre-shared keys—all exfiltration-worthy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Following suspected FortiOS compromise (per CVE-2025-68686 timeline), hunt for anomalous use of extracted credentials: impossible-travel logins, re-authentication failures suggesting credential rotation, or use of VPN credentials from anomalous geolocations within 48h post-breach.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Malformed HTTP Requests to Vulnerable Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the direct attack vector and pipeline generated zero detections for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS access logs for anomalous or malformed HTTP requests targeting known-vulnerable versions. Alert on path-traversal-like syntax, oversized headers, null bytes, or unusual query parameters in requests to admin/management interfaces. Correlate with asset inventory flagging unpatched FortiOS instances to identify at-risk targets.

suggestion.title: Symlink Persistence Mechanism Bypass Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—post-breach persistence detection is entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for symlink creation, modification, or resolution anomalies in FortiOS system directories post-compromise. Alert on filesystem writes to startup/initialization paths that circumvent symlink-patch validation. Monitor for file-access patterns showing both direct-path and symlink-variant access to the same resource.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—no detection use case for data leakage or anomalous access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate FortiOS data access patterns (config reads, credential-store queries) and alert on outliers post-compromise: unusual volume/frequency of sensitive file reads, bulk data transfers, or egress to external/unwhitelisted infrastructure. Escalate any multi-GB transfers from compromised FortiOS instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Unpatched Asset Detection (Patch Due 2026-08-10)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'patch lag is the silent killer'—pipeline should flag scanner correlation for this specific CVE and federal due-date enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for unpatched FortiOS versions matching CVE-2025-68686. Validate patch compliance via version queries and configuration inspection. Alert on any non-compliant instances found after federal due date (2026-08-10) per CISA mandate.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Devices (CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker exploits via 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the patch. This is the attack vector and detection point. No use case was generated despite this being the primary observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliances (via Web Access Logs / IDS / WAF logs) for HTTP requests exhibiting exploit signatures or anomalous patterns targeting CVE-2025-68686. Baseline normal admin traffic and alert on deviation. Prioritize unauthenticated requests that probe sensitive URIs or contain path traversal indicators.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure / Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: CVE title contains 'Exposure of Sensitive Information'—this is the vulnerability class. Pipeline should have generated detections for data exfiltration or unauthorized file access from FortiOS instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for large or unusual data transfers from FortiOS appliances post-exploitation. Monitor for reads of sensitive configuration files (e.g., `.db`, credential stores, policy backups) followed by network egress. Cross-reference with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Traversal / Filesystem Persistence on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is a 'bypass [of the patch developed for the] symbolic link persistency mechanism' and requires 'filesystem level' access. This indicates post-exploitation filesystem abuse that should be detected separately from initial HTTP exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS hosts, detect creation or modification of symbolic links in expected application directories or sensitive paths. Monitor filesystem events for unusual link creation attempts that point outside normal directory structures. Correlate timeline with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation events.

suggestion.title: Pre-Patch Vulnerability Exploitation Chain (CVE-2025-68686 Prerequisite)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This two-stage chain (initial compromise → CVE-2025-68686) should generate a hunt for the first-stage vulnerability. Pipeline missed this dependency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FortiOS instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 with historical vulnerability scans to identify what prior CVE may have granted filesystem access. Hunt for exploitation of Fortinet 0-days or known FortiOS RCEs in the same timeframe on the same hosts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Before Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10 and notes CISA KEV status means active exploitation. Patch compliance is the baseline control for any exploited CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2025-68686 present on FortiOS instances. Cross-reference with patch management system to identify unpatched assets. Flag any FortiOS system missing the patch after federal due date (2026-08-10) as critical risk.

suggestion.title: Detect Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting FortiOS Symbolic Link Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the exploitation vector—detecting malformed or unusual HTTP requests to FortiOS is necessary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS web logs and IDS telemetry for HTTP requests with unexpected headers, methods, or payloads targeting known bypass endpoints. Look for requests that may attempt to manipulate file paths or bypass validation checks related to symbolic link handling.

suggestion.title: Detect Filesystem-Level Symbolic Link Persistence Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' at filesystem level. Direct filesystem monitoring for suspicious symbolic link creation is a host-based detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem events for unusual symbolic link creation in system directories, particularly paths that would allow persistence across service restarts. Flag symlinks pointing to unexpected locations or created by non-system processes.

suggestion.title: Detect Multi-Stage FortiOS Exploitation (Prerequisite Vulnerability Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Detection must account for the prerequisite exploitation required to reach the HTTP request bypass phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CVE-2025-68686 bypass attempt detection with suspicious FortiOS activity in preceding hours/days indicating exploitation of prerequisite vulnerabilities. Look for sequences: unexpected file access → privilege escalation → symbolic link creation → HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated FortiOS Access Anomalies (Bypass Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can issue the HTTP requests. Detecting unauthenticated access to sensitive FortiOS functions is a direct control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP requests to FortiOS administrative interfaces, particularly those with unusual payloads or targeting paths associated with file handling, symbolic link management, or configuration manipulation.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Bypassing FortiOS Symlink Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' No detection hypothesis provided despite this being the core exploit technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP request logs for patterns targeting patch-related endpoints, especially those with path-traversal sequences, null-byte injection, or symlink-specific payloads. Correlate spikes in 40x responses to known patch versions with subsequent data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the exploitation vector. No hunt for detecting symlink creation post-compromise in FortiOS directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect filesystem events creating symbolic links in FortiOS application, config (/etc/init.d, systemd), or script directories. Baseline legitimate symlinks; alert on new targets, unusual ownership, or creation timestamps correlating with network exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Following FortiOS Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No detection case provided for identifying exfiltration in network or host telemetry post-bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual egress from FortiOS processes: large file transfers to external IPs, compression/encryption of config/credential storage post-patch-bypass attempt, or SOCKS proxy establishment from FortiOS daemon.

suggestion.title: Account Manipulation or Token Hijacking on Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' No detection hypothesis for account takeover or session escalation following initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After filesystem-level compromise, detect new administrative accounts created in FortiOS, privilege escalations via crafted requests, or abnormal session tokens issued to compromised accounts. Correlate account creation timing with exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Browser Extension Context Escape - Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'flaw let malicious sites read WhatsApp Web data.' Requires detection for extension APIs being invoked from untrusted JavaScript context to access browser storage, DOM, or inter-frame messages tied to messaging platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser processes loading Adobe Acrobat extension followed by in-page JavaScript (from non-Adobe domains) calling extension message APIs or accessing localStorage keys matching messaging app patterns (e.g., 'wa_*', 'whatsapp*'). Correlate with unusual outbound connections from extension process.

suggestion.title: Drive-by Compromise via Malicious Website
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious sites' deliver the exploit. Need detection for users landing on low-reputation domains that trigger immediate extension exploitation without explicit user action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag browser navigation to domains with recent registration, no SSL certificate authority reputation, or phishing-related DNS registrations followed within seconds by unexpected Adobe Acrobat extension network activity or DOM inspection patterns.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of WhatsApp Web Data via Web Connection
suggestion.rationale: Article states data was 'read' from WhatsApp Web, implying extraction. Detect ex-filtration of conversation metadata, contacts, or message content to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests from browser or Adobe extension processes containing serialized WhatsApp Web data structures (contact lists, message timestamps, conversation UUIDs) to non-Meta/non-Cloudflare infrastructure. Flag large data volumes (>1MB) to unknown C2 domains within 60s of WhatsApp Web access.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Adobe Acrobat Browser Extension Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies a 'flaw' in the extension enabling unauthorized access. Detection needed for successful exploit execution and privilege escalation into extension context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes executing JavaScript from external sites that instantiate Adobe extension objects and invoke APIs outside documented public interface. Monitor for extension process crashes followed by data access indicators, or for successful execution of exploit payloads matching known Adobe extension bypass techniques.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Execution from Untrusted Domain Accessing Extension Internals
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires hostile JavaScript executing in browser context with capability to call extension APIs. Article phrase 'malicious sites' confirms third-party script execution as vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web pages served from non-Adobe domains whose inline or externally-loaded JavaScript successfully calls adobe.extension.* or chrome.runtime.connect() APIs, or reads/writes to extension background page objects. Flag when Content Security Policy violations correlate with extension API calls.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Same-Origin Policy Bypass via Extension Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: WhatsApp Web data theft without explicit DOM access indicates SOP bypass via extension context. Detect when non-messaging-domain requests successfully access web.whatsapp.com resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XMLHttpRequest/fetch calls originating from HTML pages on external attacker-controlled domains that successfully reach web.whatsapp.com API endpoints or IndexedDB storage. Correlate with absence of browser SOP warnings or bypass of CORS headers via extension background script.

suggestion.title: Detect installation of compromised @joyfill npm packages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names @joyfill/components and @joyfill/layouts as compromised packages in public npm registry; pipeline extracted zero package IOCs. This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install or yarn add operations for @joyfill/components or @joyfill/layouts from public npm registry. Correlate with deployment systems and developer machines. Confirm compromised versions via package manifest timestamps post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: Detect obfuscated code execution within node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'obfuscated remote access trojan'—pipeline did not generate detection for obfuscated code execution (T1027), which is the core attack technique after installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js runtime for execution of base64-encoded, gzip-compressed, or otherwise obfuscated strings in require() chains or eval() patterns. Flag suspicious child processes spawned from node_modules/@joyfill subdirectories or from require() of these packages.

suggestion.title: Detect RAT command-and-control communication from Node.js processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a remote access trojan; pipeline missed C2 detection logic. RATs must phone home; network-based detection is critical. Article should specify C2 indicators if available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of network destinations contacted by legitimate @joyfill packages. Alert on anomalous outbound connections (non-RFC1918 addresses, high-entropy domains, command-protocol patterns, beaconing behavior) from Node.js or child processes post-installation.

suggestion.title: Detect persistence installation by npm package code
suggestion.rationale: RATs universally establish persistence; article likely describes persistence techniques but pipeline generated no detection. Supply-chain malware typically plants scheduled tasks, registry keys, or startup scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU RUN keys, scheduled task creation (Win32_ScheduledJob, Task Scheduler), and file writes to Startup folders during or immediately after @joyfill package installation. Cross-reference parent process to npm/Node.js.

suggestion.title: Detect privilege escalation attempts from npm package context
suggestion.rationale: RATs frequently attempt privilege escalation; pipeline did not propose detections for escalation techniques (T1134, T1547, etc.) that malicious npm code would employ.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UAC elevation prompts, token impersonation attempts, or WMI/COM elevation patterns originating from Node.js processes or child processes spawned by @joyfill code. Correlate with package installation timeline.

suggestion.title: Detect system reconnaissance commands from npm-spawned child processes
suggestion.rationale: RATs perform discovery (T1049, T1082, T1087); pipeline did not propose detection for reconnaissance activity that typically follows successful initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of whoami, ipconfig, tasklist, systeminfo, net commands or their PowerShell equivalents as child processes of Node.js. Flag unusual combinations or rapid execution consistent with automated discovery scripts.

suggestion.title: SFTP file access operations following goshs connection from non-standard port
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SFTP accepts connections without password' and implies file transfer via SFTP after auth bypass. Need detection for successful SFTP sessions followed by file read/write operations. Article provides no file-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SFTP SSH handshake completion (successful auth, possibly with empty password signature) on non-standard ports (e.g., 2222) with subsequent file I/O operations from the SFTP process. Flag if source is external or privileged-access tool.

suggestion.title: goshs process invoked with -b flag containing empty username or password segment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vuln config: `-b 'admin:'` (empty password after colon) and earlier CVE as `:pass` (empty username before colon). The regex in UC_4_2 covers this, but a complementary hunt for command-line argument parsing of the `-b` flag itself would catch missed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on goshs/goshs.exe process creation where ProcessCommandLine contains `-b` followed by pattern matching `<username>:` (no password) OR `:<password>` (no username), excluding processes with `-fkf` flag.

suggestion.title: goshs configuration file creation or modification with empty-credential basic auth
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions vulnerability config passed via `-b` flag; if config is persisted to file (e.g., `.goshs.conf`), detect file write/modification events with empty credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of goshs config files (common patterns: `.goshs.conf`, `goshs.yaml`, `goshs.json`) where file content contains `-b` flag with empty username or password segment, or direct config key `basic_auth` with null/empty password value.

suggestion.title: SSH service fingerprint mismatch: goshs SFTP variant detected via banner or protocol anomaly
suggestion.rationale: goshs is a lightweight SFTP server with distinct SSH banner and protocol behavior; network detection can identify unexpected/unauthorized goshs instances. Article does not mention network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SSH connections with Server Banner containing 'goshs' or exhibiting SFTP-only protocol behavior (no interactive shell) from unexpected/unauthorized hosts or listening on non-standard ports (e.g., 2222).

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Exploited SmartConsole Flaw Allowing Full Admin Access'—implies unauthorized access to management console, the critical initial vector for this vulnerability chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole for authentication bypasses or HTTP requests to /web/index.html and /smartconsole endpoints that succeed without valid credentials. Flag requests using known exploit patterns or from unexpected source IPs/ASNs.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation via SmartConsole Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly states 'Full Admin Access'—post-exploitation, attacker will create privileged accounts for persistence. Yet pipeline generated no detection for unauthorized admin account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new administrative user creation in SmartConsole outside normal provisioning windows, especially following suspicious authentication events or during off-hours. Flag accounts with implicit trust relationships to managed security appliances.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole API Abuse for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised SmartConsole with admin privileges enables unrestricted access to managed Check Point gateways via REST API (/web_api/v*). Pipeline missed detection for command-and-control via management plane.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole REST API calls for unusual patterns: bulk policy deployments, gateway configuration changes, rule insertions, or API authentication from new user agents/IPs. Correlate with newly-created admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Security Policy Deployment via SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: With admin access, attacker modifies firewall rules on all managed appliances. Headline implies 'full admin access' includes policy control—this is an impact vector the pipeline completely ignored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy pushes that disable logging, add overly-permissive rules (e.g., allow-all to specific IPs), or modify inspection profiles on bulk appliances. Flag policy changes occurring outside change windows or by recently-provisioned admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Firewall Gateway Compromise via SmartConsole Chain
suggestion.rationale: SmartConsole admin access enables compromise of all downstream Check Point appliances. Article's 'full admin access' directly threatens managed gateway security posture—no lateral movement UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for configuration synchronization events from SmartConsole to gateways that contain suspicious commands or policy rules. Alert on unexpected gateway restarts, certificate changes, or firmware updates initiated from compromised SmartConsole.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Version Scanning and Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Before exploitation, attackers enumerate SmartConsole versions to confirm vulnerability presence. Article states 'patches exploited'—implies active reconnaissance phase missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to SmartConsole endpoints that probe for version info (/web/help/about, JS version strings, default paths). Flag rapid version enumeration attempts from single source IP followed by exploitation patterns within 24–48 hours.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Scanner Validation Against KEV
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Even if your scanners say "not vulnerable" because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet' — scanners may miss the known-exploited status or patch-bypass logic. Needs active validation against CISA KEV confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FortiOS devices are reported 'patched' against CVE-2025-68686 but are still exposed to the known-exploited form (patch bypass via symlink persistence). Compare scanner output against CISA KEV publication date (2026-07-27) to identify lag.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symlink Persistence Mechanism Filesystem Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and 'at filesystem level' — post-compromise attackers will create or manipulate symlinks to bypass patched HTTP handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (especially /etc, /var, /tmp) for symlink creation or modification correlated with HTTP daemon restarts or crafted HTTP requests. Symlink targets pointing to sensitive config or system paths warrant escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management/Web Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and 'via crafted HTTP requests' as the exploitation vector post-compromise — malformed or unusual HTTP patterns bypass the patched symlink check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS web/management ports (80, 443, 8443) from external IPs that are malformed (oversized headers, null bytes, unusual path traversal attempts, symlink-escape sequences) without authentication headers. Correlate with symlink filesystem events.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Information Disclosure Post-Compromise via HTTP Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' through the patch bypass — successful exploitation results in data exfiltration from config files, logs, or system state accessible via symlinks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large reads or exfiltration of sensitive FortiOS files (/etc/system.conf, /etc/passwd, /var/log/*, certificate stores) following patched HTTP daemon activity or after symlink creation. Monitor for encoded/compressed data staging on the filesystem.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypasses via Known Symlink Escape Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' — the patch itself is known; look for HTTP payloads that work around it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match HTTP request payloads against known PoC patterns for CVE-2025-68686 symlink bypass (e.g., double-URL encoding of ../../../, null-byte injection, symlink-race conditions). Correlate payload attempts with 404/403 responses followed by 200 OK responses on sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Fileless FortiOS Post-Exploitation via Memory-Mapped Symlinks
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — once inside, symlink abuse may enable memory-resident persistence without disk artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FortiOS HTTP daemon (e.g., httpsd) opening symlinked files or mapping them to memory; correlate with /proc/<PID>/maps changes or unusual system calls (openat, readlink, mmap) that re-read symlinked config files at runtime.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation in the wild; 'CVE-2025-68686... only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Federal patch due 2026-08-10. Vulnerability scanner data is primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS appliances (FortiGate, FortiManager, etc.) missing patches for CVE-2025-68686 via vulnerability scanner output or asset inventory. Cross-reference with patch dates post-2026-08-10 federal deadline. False positives: scanner false negatives on patched builds.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—persistence vector used post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (via sysmon, auditd, or FortiOS CLI logs) for suspicious symbolic link creation in system directories or config paths. Look for unusual .lnk or symlink references in /etc, /opt, or application directories post-compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting FortiOS Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits 'via crafted HTTP requests' after filesystem-level access—exploitation delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS management ports (443, 8080, 10443) with malformed headers, oversized payloads, or unusual URI patterns. Correlate with failed auth attempts or file-modification events on same system within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Filesystem Modification on Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—behavioral detection post-initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect filesystem writes to FortiOS system binaries, config files, or boot-level paths by non-admin processes or unexpected service accounts. Escalate if modification timestamp post-dates known vulnerability exploitation window.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Drift Post-Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-08-10 is audit trigger; 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Regulatory compliance reporting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-2026-08-10: identify FortiOS instances still missing CVE-2025-68686 patches. Flag as audit-reportable non-compliance. Cross-check against CISA KEV due-date tracker to identify remediation gaps.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Public-Facing Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can exploit 'public-facing application' — this is T1190 in practice. Pipeline missed explicit attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for HTTP requests to management interfaces from external sources. Baseline normal admin access patterns and alert on spike in authentication failures or unusual source IPs. Focus on unauthenticated access attempts to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypass via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'crafted HTTP requests' used to 'bypass the patch' — this is the core exploitation technique. Pipeline failed to operationalize this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests with suspicious payloads targeting FortiOS HTTP handlers. Look for requests with unusual character encoding, path traversal patterns, or oversized headers that may bypass WAF/IDS signatures. Correlate against known CVE-2025-68686 PoC patterns.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — this describes T1547/T1574 persistence, not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation or modification of symlinks in sensitive directories (config, bin, lib paths). Detect symlink→external paths. Alert on symlinks created within 10 minutes of exploit indicator (HTTP 403→200 pattern or authentication log anomalies).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit FortiOS Sensitive Information Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker seeks 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' after initial breach — requires post-exploit monitoring for data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting initial compromise or patch bypass, hunt for access to sensitive config files (passwd, config.db, certificates) via unusual process or user context. Monitor for syslog exfiltration, unusual outbound TLS connections from FortiOS appliance, or config file reads by non-admin users.

suggestion.title: Prior Compromise Detection — Filesystem-Level FortiOS Access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — this multi-stage attack requires detection of initial filesystem compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect first-stage compromise by monitoring FortiOS OS-level file writes to protected paths (root-level binaries, config directories) by processes running as non-root or via unusual execution chains. Correlate with kernel logs for privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Patch Non-Compliance and Bypass Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context: article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and attackers exploit already-patched vulnerabilities. Detection must confirm patch presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all FortiOS instances for presence of the CVE-2025-68686 patch. Correlate patch status against HTTP attack attempts — if unpatched instance receives crafted HTTP requests, escalate immediately. Detect attempts to patch downgrade or patch-bypass via integrity checks.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FortiOS Inventory — CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet.' CISA KEV implies active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-08-10 creates hard deadline for remediation hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for FortiOS versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Flag any external-facing instances not patched before 2026-08-10. Escalate based on CVSS and network exposure.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management/API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'crafted HTTP requests' against FortiOS. This malformed HTTP traffic signature must be monitored at proxy/WAF/network-edge layers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP requests to external FortiOS admin/API endpoints for malformed payloads, oversized parameters, null bytes, or path-traversal patterns. Correlate with auth bypass (401→200 transitions) or 5xx errors.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Symlink abuse is direct persistence indicator post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation/modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (init, cron, startup, config paths). Alert on ln -s or symlink() syscalls in restricted locations. Correlate with prior compromise timestamps.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise Activity (Pre-CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This two-stage attack requires hunting for prior access: file upload, path traversal, or command injection that preceded HTTP exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate timeline: hunt FortiOS logs for file writes to unexpected paths, unsigned binary execution, privilege escalation attempts, or known CVEs (path traversal, arbitrary file write) exploited in weeks before detection of CVE-2025-68686 activity.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiOS Gateway
suggestion.rationale: A compromised firewall/gateway is network-critical pivot point. Post-breach lateral movement to internal assets must be monitored to limit blast radius.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag anomalous outbound traffic from FortiOS management/data planes to internal subnets post-compromise (SMB, RDP, LDAP, DNS queries to internal resources). Alert on new sessions to high-value targets (AD, exchange, databases).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection via Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2025-68686 as the indicator and explicitly references the asset-exposure hunt template. CISA KEV status means active exploitation; standard asset-exposure rule applies directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Fortinet FortiOS systems reporting vulnerable versions matching CVE-2025-68686 in scanner output. Cross-reference with patch due date 2026-08-10 for compliance tracking and urgency prioritization.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiOS Admin/Config Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the exploitation vector. Requires monitoring for HTTP patterns that attempt to bypass the patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiOS management interfaces for malformed requests: unusual encodings, oversized payloads, POST/PUT to config endpoints with suspicious headers, path traversal indicators (../, encoded equivalents), or requests containing filesystem-level special characters.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation in FortiOS Critical Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—direct indicator of post-exploitation persistence attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS config directories, web root, or module paths. Establish baseline of authorized symlinks and flag new ones outside maintenance windows, especially those pointing to sensitive files or system utilities.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Credentials and Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—direct impact. Monitor who/what accesses credential stores post-detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reads of FortiOS configuration files (config.sys), credential vaults, VPN secret storage, and admin user databases. Flag access patterns that do not match baseline (non-admin processes, HTTP handlers, scheduled tasks accessing these files).

suggestion.title: Bypass of CVE-2025-68686 Patch via HTTP Evasion Techniques
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—indicates active evasion. Detect requests that successfully evade patch protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests employing alternate encodings, request smuggling, chunked transfer encoding tricks, or filesystem-level escape sequences designed to reach code paths supposedly protected by the CVE-2025-68686 patch. Correlate successful exploitation with symlink creation or credential access.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerable Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates hunt for exposed FortiOS instances: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...#asset-exposure]'. Pipeline generated zero use cases. Article explicitly references Fortinet FortiOS product and CVE-2025-68686.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances exposed to internet via port 443/80 scanning, banner grabbing, or vulnerability scanner results. Use vendor identification string matching in proxy logs, IDS/IPS signatures, or active network discovery. Correlate against CVE-2025-68686 patch status.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt (Crafted HTTP Requests)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests'. Pipeline failed to create detection for this exploitation vector despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances (identified via product discovery) for malformed or anomalous HTTP requests targeting known exploitation paths. Flag requests with unusual header combinations, path traversal patterns, or symlink-related payloads. Correlate with post-compromise filesystem access patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem Persistence Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'filesystem level' compromise as prerequisite. Pipeline missed detection for persistence artifacts left behind post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiOS systems for symbolic links created in unexpected locations (especially web-accessible directories), unusual file ownership changes, or suspicious .so / binary modifications in system paths. Cross-reference against patched vs. unpatched asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'. Pipeline generated no detection for the information disclosure phase despite it being the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unauthorized read access to sensitive FortiOS files (e.g., config archives, VPN credentials, encrypted keys) by correlating filesystem audit logs with HTTP request logs. Flag exfiltration of large config files or repeated access to credential stores on CVE-2025-68686 affected instances.

suggestion.title: Pre-Requisite Vulnerability Chain Leading to CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'. Pipeline failed to model the prerequisite compromise as part of the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each FortiOS instance, cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results to identify other active CVEs or unpatched services that could serve as initial entry point. Prioritize instances with multiple vulnerabilities present. Model attack chain as: [initial CVE] → [filesystem access] → [CVE-2025-68686 exploitation] → [info disclosure].

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request to FortiOS Sensitive Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism... via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the active exploitation vector and should be a first-order detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin/API endpoints for HTTP requests with atypical patterns: path traversal sequences, unusual HTTP methods, malformed headers, or parameters that bypass validation. Correlate with Fortinet OS version to flag unpatched targets. Baseline legitimate admin and automation traffic first to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation in FortiOS Config/Data Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the underlying post-exploit technique being bypassed. Direct filesystem monitoring for symlink creation is the persistence hunting signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation (ln -s, mklink, or API equivalent) in FortiOS critical directories: /var/lib, /var/etc, /opt/fortinet, /var/log. Filter out maintenance symlinks (config backups, log rotation). Correlate with prior filesystem access from non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Must detect access to FortiOS secrets post-compromise: keys, credentials, VPN configs, traffic logs stored at filesystem level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor read access to /var/log (traffic/auth logs), /var/etc/admin_* (admin hashes), /var/etc/certs (private keys), /var/etc/vpn (VPN configs) from non-FortiOS-service processes. Alert on bulk exfil patterns (multiple files read in short window from single process).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry mandates scanner-based detection. Article specifies CVE-2025-68686 and federal patch-due date 2026-08-10. Any unpatched FortiOS in scope is a critical alert.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) for CVE-2025-68686 matches. Alert on High/Critical findings on externally-facing FortiOS instances. Cross-reference with patch management system to confirm remediation status and prioritize by patch gap (due date: 2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Filesystem Access Followed by Anomalous HTTP Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain: compromise (filesystem-level access) → then HTTP-based exploitation. Detecting the correlation between filesystem modifications and subsequent crafted HTTP requests is the two-stage exploit signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate (a) filesystem-level write/create events in FortiOS system dirs with (b) anomalous HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints within 5-30 minutes. Baseline: legitimate admin changes to FortiOS config are typically via CLI or API, not raw filesystem writes. Alert on write→HTTP correlation, especially if source is non-admin process.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Admin/API Access from Non-Standard Clients
suggestion.rationale: Prior compromise required for exploitation. After initial breach, attacker must interact with FortiOS remotely—likely via REST API or admin interface. Look for authentication from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin interface (port 443, /admin path) and REST API (port 443, /api/v2) for login attempts and API calls from IPs not in baseline (datacenter IPs, known mgmt networks). Alert on failed auth attempts followed by successful access (brute force hypothesis). Flag API calls from automated tools not in change-mgmt system.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and 'patch lag is the silent killer'—requires scanning FortiOS versions across the fleet. Zero detection UCs for patch-status validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset DB for FortiOS appliances. Flag instances with version/patch dates prior to 2026-08-10. Cross-reference against CVSS score and device exposure (internet-facing). Alert on unpatched FortiOS in federal/critical-infrastructure networks.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Bypass Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'bypass the patch…via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection for malformed/adversarial HTTP patterns targeting the patch mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS web interface (typically port 443/8443) for HTTP requests with atypical structure: oversized headers, null bytes, path-traversal sequences, or symbolic-link references in URI. Alert on repeated requests to /api or config endpoints from unauthenticated sessions, especially post-IPS/vulnerability-scan activity.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—no detection for filesystem artifacts created after initial compromise. This is the persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS /var, /tmp, and /proc for symbolic links to auth binaries, config parsers, or credential stores. Alert on ln -s or symlink syscalls from non-standard processes outside change-management windows. Correlate with prior filesystem write events and HTTP request anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Sensitive Data Access from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker'…'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No detection for unauthorized data reads/exfiltration without valid session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS audit logs for file reads from /etc/passwd equivalents, VPN config dirs, certificate keystores, and credential vaults. Alert on data access without valid admin session, especially followed by outbound HTTP/HTTPS to non-Fortinet IPs. Correlate with prior symlink-creation events.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vulnerability Exploitation Chain (Initial CVE → FortiOS Filesystem Access → CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' No detection for the two-stage attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate events within 48-hour windows: (1) failed scanner detection for unrelated FortiOS CVE or IPS alert, (2) filesystem writes to /var or /tmp, (3) HTTP bypass requests or symlink artifacts. Flag devices showing this sequence as high-confidence multi-stage exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Configuration/Certificate Exfiltration via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Core impact: 'exposure of sensitive information.' Post-exploitation typically involves config/credential dumps. No detection for outbound exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress from FortiOS for large HTTP PUT/POST to external IPs containing base64, gzip, or plaintext patterns matching FortiOS config markers ('config system', 'set password', PEM certificate headers). Alert on certificate material or credential hashes leaving the appliance.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests—CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker… via crafted HTTP requests' to FortiOS management interface; canonical initial-access vector not captured
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS web interface traffic (ports 80/443, 8080 typical) for anomalous HTTP patterns: high density of 40x errors from single source, POST requests with suspicious parameter encoding, or requests to known-vulnerable API endpoints. Establish baseline benign admin traffic before alerting.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Inventory Sweep
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-08-10. Article mentions 'patch developed for symbolic link persistency,' indicating multiple firmware versions affected
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all FortiOS instances against CVE-2025-68686 affected versions (typically 6.x/7.x branches). Alert on any system running unpatched build; correlate with active network reachability and exposure (WAN-facing vs. internal-only). Validate patch installation post-remediation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FortiOS Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Following exploitation chain, attackers will target credentials, session tokens, config files
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS egress traffic for large data transfers to non-enterprise IPs; detect file access patterns targeting /etc, config backup paths, or credential stores. Correlate with preceding exploitation attempts. Alert on compression/encryption of sensitive filetypes shortly after successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass or Patch Validation Failure—Symbolic Link Persistency
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—indicates attackers re-exploiting code paths security teams believed patched
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-patch, monitor FortiOS for evidence of symlink-based access to protected files or directories. Alert on repeated 403/permission-denied events followed by successful traversal. Detect patch rollback or downgrade; validate patch integrity via checksum comparison against vendor builds.

suggestion.title: Prerequisite Vulnerability Exploitation on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—detection of the staging attack required
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for exploitation of known FortiOS pre-conditions (other CVEs in same product family, or filesystem-level access methods—SSH, SNMP, etc.). Correlate filesystem modifications or privilege escalation events immediately preceding HTTP-based exploitation attempts. Timeline clustering of distinct exploit payloads.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'match against your vulnerability scanner for CVE-2025-68686' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal remediation due 2026-08-10. Asset exposure hunt is canonical for any KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 (unpatched versions). Cross-correlate scanner output with network asset inventory; flag instances reachable from untrusted networks. Alert on scanner detection anomalies (scanners reporting 'patched' when version numbers contradict).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation vector: 'remote unauthenticated attacker...via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline must surface detection for malformed/anomalous HTTP payloads targeting FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiOS admin/API endpoints for payloads with anomalous structure, path traversal attempts, or symlink-escape patterns. Alert on repeated failed exploit attempts or request clustering suggesting automated scanning.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Abuse and Filesystem Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — direct evidence of T1547 persistence post-compromise. Filesystem access patterns must be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system for symlink creation/modification in sensitive directories (config paths, plugin directories, script locations). Alert on symlinks pointing to world-writable locations or user-controlled paths. Correlate with prior access anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability core behavior: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Must detect abnormal reads/exports of credentials, configs, keys, or logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unauthorized file access to /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, config files, VPN credential storage, firewall rules, and logs. Flag API calls or tool invocations that bulk-export or exfiltrate sensitive data. Correlate access patterns with exploit timeframes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypass Indicators and Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Must detect patch rollbacks, permission manipulations, or code overwrites that neutralize mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor patch application logs for rollbacks, failed patch installs, or permission changes post-patching. Alert if version reports show patch applied but vulnerable code paths remain executable. Flag suspicious modifications to patch files or security modules.

suggestion.title: Prior Vulnerability Compromise Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Multi-CVE compromise pattern must be detected; first compromise is the true initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference FortiOS instances targeted for CVE-2025-68686 exploitation against related known Fortinet CVEs (symlink path traversal, privilege escalation, LPE). Flag instances with filesystem-level access signatures predating CVE-2025-68686 activity. Correlate with intrusion feed intelligence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Detection for Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests.' No UC generated to detect anomalous HTTP traffic patterns targeting FortiOS with malformed or suspicious payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for requests with unusual parameter encoding, directory traversal patterns, or oversized payloads. Baseline normal admin traffic and alert on deviations that may indicate patch-bypass attempts using crafted requests.

suggestion.title: Symlink Persistence Post-Compromise on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—indicating attackers establish persistence via symlinks after initial compromise. No UC addresses symlink creation/modification detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on filesystem events showing symlink creation in FortiOS critical directories (/etc, /bin, /opt/fortinet) pointing to writable or user-accessible locations. Correlate with prior exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation Detection: Multi-Vulnerability FortiOS Attack Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—describes a two-stage attack chain. Pipeline missed detection of sequential exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple exploitation attempts against different known FortiOS CVEs within short timeframes, or failed auth attempts followed by filesystem access indicators, to identify attackers chaining vulnerabilities for deep compromise.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Information Access Following FortiOS Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—the impact phase. No UC to detect suspicious data access patterns post-exploitation, such as unusual log queries or config file reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS logs for unusual read access to sensitive config files, credentials, or logs by unauthenticated or low-privilege processes. Baseline normal admin queries and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Release Tag Re-pointed to Orphaned Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' — tags like v35 re-pointed to attack commit not on any branch
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags in high-dependency repositories (e.g., >1000 downstream dependents) are deleted or re-pointed to commits not on main/release branches, especially if commits have no recent branch ancestry or author is unusual.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Direct Reference in Workflow Logs
suggestion.rationale: Attack feasibility requires: 'commit orphaned from any branches' yet 'you can still navigate to that commit' — orphaned commits accessible after branch deletion enable stealthy persistence
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow logs and Git audit logs for commit references that exist in external integrations but are not reachable from any current branch; flag if orphaned commits are executed in Actions pipelines or referenced in releases.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secret Exposure in GitHub Actions Job Logs
suggestion.rationale: Direct impact stated: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs' — secrets leaked to public logs due to compromised Action code
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions job logs (especially public repos) for high-entropy strings matching AWS key patterns, GitHub tokens (ghp_, ghu_, ghr_), or other credential formats. Correlate with repository secret definitions to confirm false exposure vs. intentional logging.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Call from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: Attack detection method: 'made an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from GitHub Actions runner subnets to non-whitelisted external domains, particularly curl/wget/git operations fetching code from non-repository sources. Compare against baseline for given Action repository.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to package.json dependencies, new entries in scripts field, or bin field modifications pointing to obfuscated payloads. Flag commits modifying package manifests outside normal development branches.

suggestion.title: Database Query Log SQL Injection Detection (ClickHouse/PostgreSQL/MySQL)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'inject arbitrary SQL' via 'trailing backslash to escape the closing quote' in parameters. Database query audit logs would show malformed escaping patterns. This is where actual exploitation is visible, not web traffic. Missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search database query logs for SQL patterns with escaped quotes and backslashes in parameter substitution contexts. Look for statements where closing quotes are preceded by backslashes (e.g., `WHERE id = \'...\`), indicating successful escaping bypass. Correlate with error logs showing SQL parse errors if the injection failed.

suggestion.title: Application Error Log: @hypequery/clickhouse Parameter Parsing Failures
suggestion.rationale: When an attacker sends a crafted parameter with a trailing backslash, the library's `escapeValue()` function processes it. Failed or unusual escaping attempts may emit structured error logs, warnings, or exceptions in application logs. Article mentions 'escapeValue() function' and parameter handling but pipeline missed application-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for error logs or exceptions mentioning 'hypequery', 'clickhouse', 'escapeValue', 'quote', 'backslash', or 'escape failure'. Anomalously frequent parameter parsing errors within a short timespan may indicate exploitation attempts. Correlate with network egress from affected hosts.

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Scanning: Inventory of @hypequery/clickhouse Installations
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies versions < 2.0.2 are vulnerable. Pipeline's UC_2_2 handles this via TVM, but misses npm package manager auditing (package-lock.json, yarn.lock), which provides a first line of detection in development and deployment pipelines before TVM scans catch it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm lock files and package managers for @hypequery/clickhouse versions < 2.0.2. Flag all host/container images that include the vulnerable package. Escalate if found in production or user-facing services.

suggestion.title: API Parameter Injection via Proxy/WAF Logs (Non-Web-Query Context)
suggestion.rationale: UC_2_1 searches URL parameters, but ClickHouse is often accessed via programmatic clients or internal APIs where SQL injection payloads appear in POST bodies, JSON payloads, or gRPC messages, not URL query strings. Article does not limit exploitation to web URLs, but pipeline detection does.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search proxy and API gateway logs for POST/PUT requests to ClickHouse-adjacent endpoints (or requests that later correlate with database errors) containing parameter values with backslash-quote patterns (raw or encoded). Look for requests from unexpected sources or with abnormal payloads.

suggestion.title: WebDAV file deletion signaled by failed DELETE + successful MOVE on same path
suggestion.rationale: Article's core finding: 'DELETE is correctly blocked (403) but MOVE still destroys existing files, defeating the documented [--no-delete policy].' This mismatch is the exploit signature. Detecting 403 on DELETE followed by 204 on MOVE for identical resources within seconds identifies bypass attempts.
log_sources: HTTP access logs with full verb and status
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to the same URL path where DELETE returns 403 and MOVE (within 60 seconds) returns 204 No Content. This pattern indicates an attacker probing the no-delete restriction, finding it bypassed by MOVE, and exploiting it.

suggestion.title: WebDAV MOVE with Overwrite: T header targeting --no-delete configurations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'with `Overwrite: T` it additionally performs an explicit `RemoveAll` on the destination.' This header is the mechanism enabling the bypass. Direct detection of Overwrite: T on MOVE verbs sent to goshs instances configured with --no-delete is high-fidelity.
log_sources: Web proxy logs with header capture
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP MOVE requests with the header 'Overwrite: T' (or 'Overwrite: true') sent to endpoints known to be goshs with --no-delete flag active. This header should cause 403 Forbidden but does not due to the CVE, making requests returning 204 actionable.

suggestion.title: Filesystem file deletion/removal events correlated with WebDAV MOVE 204 responses
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the payload: 'MOVE deletes the source file' and 'RemoveAll on the destination.' Impact confirmation requires file system auditing. Correlation of successful MOVE responses (204) with subsequent filesystem deletions (unlink/remove events) proves exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems where goshs runs, correlate Web server log entries for HTTP 204 on MOVE verbs with filesystem auditing events showing inode/file removal on the targeted paths within 5 seconds. This combination confirms the vulnerability resulted in actual data loss.

suggestion.title: WebDAV directory enumeration showing missing resources post-MOVE exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Data destruction impact (T1485) can be confirmed by comparing WebDAV directory listings before and after MOVE operations. Resources deleted by the bypass will no longer appear in PROPFIND responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track WebDAV PROPFIND requests (directory listings) before and after successful MOVE 204 responses. Cross-reference directory contents; a file present in the first listing should disappear in the second, indicating successful exploitation and file destruction.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin Access via SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Full Admin Access' as the impact. Pipeline should have generated detection for privilege escalation to admin on Check Point management interfaces. No use case present despite criticality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole servers for successful authentication followed by immediate elevation to admin privileges or role changes. Flag accounts that gain admin access outside normal maintenance windows or from unexpected source IPs. Correlate failed auth attempts followed by successful admin-level API calls.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Exploited SmartConsole Flaw'—pipeline should have generated detection for the exploitation path itself, not just post-compromise admin access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole ports (typically 4434, 18190) for exploit-pattern traffic, such as malformed HTTP requests, SQL injection payloads in SmartConsole API parameters, or auth bypass patterns. Flag requests that bypass or circumvent SmartConsole's API authentication layers.

suggestion.title: Check Point Management Server Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Full admin access would allow attacker to modify policies, user accounts, and security settings. No detection hypothesis generated for suspicious admin-level configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole audit logs and event logs for admin-level changes to security policies, firewall rules, user account creations/elevations, or credential resets.
