Flag bulk policy changes, disablement of logging, or addition of backdoor admin accounts during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch... via crafted HTTP requests'—direct signal for HTTP anomaly detection against FortiOS services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiOS web interfaces (commonly port 443, 8000, 8443) with suspicious patterns: malformed headers, oversized payloads, repeated 4xx responses followed by successful authentication, or requests containing common bypass patterns (path traversal, encoding tricks). Correlate with FortiOS version matching CVE-2025-68686 timeline.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Manipulation Post-Compromise on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'bypass the patch... symbolic link persistency'—indicates attacker leverages symlinks for persistence or privilege escalation after initial filesystem-level access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS file system operations for symlink creation (ln -s commands), symlink modifications, or access patterns through symlinked paths. Look for symlinks pointing to sensitive configuration files (/etc/passwd-equivalent, FortiOS admin credentials files). Baseline normal symlink activity and alert on anomalous creation timing or targeting sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-FortiOS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' and requires 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—indicates detection of data access/exfil after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting FortiOS compromise indicators, monitor for bulk data access to sensitive files (configuration exports, certificate stores, VPN credential stores). Alert on unexpected outbound connections from FortiOS to external IPs, especially over non-standard ports, or large unencrypted data transfers post-compromise.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Configuration Export/Backup Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sensitive information exists on FortiOS systems ('exposure of sensitive information')—attackers post-compromise typically exfiltrate configurations, certificates, or VPN credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FortiOS configuration backups or exports triggered outside maintenance windows. Alert on API calls or CLI commands initiating config dumps, especially from non-standard administrative sessions or after failed authentication attempts. Cross-reference with user activity logs to identify unauthorized export initiators.

suggestion.title: Failed-to-Successful FortiOS Authentication Chain
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV listing means active exploitation—successful attacks often show repeated auth failures before bypass succeeds via vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed HTTP authentication attempts to FortiOS (401/403 responses) with subsequent successful logins from the same source IP within short timeframe (minutes). Alert on successful admin logins following patterns consistent with exploit payloads (unusual User-Agent, malformed requests preceding auth success).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Detection Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'CVE: CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner'; pipeline output must surface this for scanner tuning and asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit vulnerability scanner results for Fortinet FortiOS assets; flag any systems where scanner reports 'not vulnerable' to CVE-2025-68686 despite firmware version falling in vulnerable range. Cross-validate with actual FortiOS version from management interfaces—patch lag and scanner configuration drift are primary miss vectors for CISA KEV entries.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Symlink Persistence Bypass via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the post-exploitation pattern that should trigger detection on HTTP request anomalies targeting symlink paths in FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiOS appliances for requests containing path traversal patterns (../, ..\ , symlink indicators) or unusual HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE) targeting system-sensitive endpoints. Correlate with prior filesystem access anomalies on the same asset.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem-Level Post-Compromise Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article prerequisite: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Filesystem modifications are the enabler for the symlink bypass attack and should be detected independently.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for file creation or modification events in FortiOS system directories (/usr/local/fcwf/, /etc/fortisandbox/, /var/log/) outside maintenance windows. Prioritize symlink file entries and changes to configuration or library files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable FortiOS Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with 'remote unauthenticated attacker' access and federal patch deadline 2026-08-10. Article directly states Fortinet FortiOS as vulnerable product and CVE-2025-68686 as the identifier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Fortinet FortiOS instances and obtain build/version numbers. Flag any instance with build version predating the vendor's CVE-2025-68686 patch release. Cross-reference with internet-facing appliance lists to identify exploitable exposure.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly names 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Post-exploitation, attacker will attempt to export configs, auth tokens, or session data. Article establishes this as the impact goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk export operations (backup downloads, configuration dumps, log exports) from FortiOS admin console outside scheduled maintenance. Monitor for authentication material or credential dumps leaving the appliance via HTTP/HTTPS outside trusted channels.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Service Restart or Crash Recovery Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence bypass activity may involve service restarts to re-establish or reset protections. Unusual restart patterns correlated with prior HTTP anomalies indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiOS core service restart frequency (fortid, httpsd) and alert on deviations within 1 hour of HTTP anomalies or filesystem access events. Correlate unexpected restarts with prior indicators of compromise.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthenticated Access Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' capability. Detection should surface successful or repeated auth bypass attempts against exposed FortiOS instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS login endpoints for failed auth attempts followed by successful unauthenticated access (e.g., 401 → 200 to admin paths). Alert on access to admin console endpoints without credential submission or with invalid credentials that succeed.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entries represent 'observed exploited in the wild' threats requiring federal remediation by due date (2026-08-10). CVE identifier is stated in title and body; pipeline must extract and alert on scanner hits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS instances flagged for CVE-2025-68686 in vulnerability scans. Cross-reference with asset inventory to prioritize internet-facing appliances. Validate actual patch levels against Fortinet timeline even if automated scans show remediated.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' is the attack vector requiring bypass. This is the explicit persistence technique; filesystem-level symlink creation post-exploitation is the core behavioral indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (via osquery, auditd, or FortiOS audit logs) for suspicious symlink creation in system/config directories. Correlate timing with authentication anomalies or prior exploitation attempts. Symlinks enable evasion of patch-based remediations.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is triggered 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patches. Network-level detection of suspicious request patterns is essential for catching active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiOS admin interfaces with unusual payloads, encoded symlink path references, oversized headers, or request patterns inconsistent with legitimate admin/API use. Flag requests matching post-exploitation bypass signatures.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes the vulnerability 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism,' indicating active defense evasion post-remediation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FortiOS appliances report patch application for CVE-2025-68686 but subsequent scans or behavioral indicators still detect symlink persistence mechanisms or HTTP bypass patterns. Indicates either incomplete patching or active post-patch exploitation.

suggestion.title: Chained CVE Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before CVE-2025-68686 exploitation. The initial CVE and filesystem compromise are separate detection opportunities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful exploitation of any other FortiOS CVE (especially pre-2025 disclosures) with subsequent filesystem access logs and symlink creation. Look for exploitation spike correlating with publication of this CVE.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Filesystem Access Pre-Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Attack prerequisites include 'filesystem level' compromise before symlink persistence. Detecting initial filesystem access is upstream detection opportunity the pipeline omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected shell access, unexpected user account filesystem operations, or root-level file modifications on FortiOS appliances. Establish baseline of legitimate maintenance activities; deviation + subsequent symlink creation = exploitation signal.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 — Vulnerable Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry' and 'observed exploited in the wild'. Template explicitly directs asset-exposure hunt substituting CVE-2025-68686. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Fortinet FortiOS instances with version strings vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference patch status against known-vulnerable builds. Prioritize any asset with patch-due date 2026-08-10 still unpatched post-deadline.

suggestion.title: FortiOS — Crafted HTTP Requests Bypassing Symbolic Link Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'remote unauthenticated attacker...via crafted HTTP requests' and 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Pipeline missed HTTP exploitation detection despite unauthenticated HTTP being the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiOS access logs for unusual HTTP request patterns targeting known sensitive endpoints (authentication bypass, configuration exposure). Focus on requests attempting to access symbolic link paths or exceeding typical query parameter length/complexity. Baseline against legitimate FortiOS management traffic.

suggestion.title: FortiOS — Post-Compromise Sensitive Information Disclosure via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information' and requires 'first...compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before HTTP attack succeeds. Pipeline ignored the sensitive data exfiltration phase of the two-stage attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for abnormal data volume exfiltration post-compromise, particularly configuration files, credential stores, or system logs being accessed/exfiltrated via HTTP. Correlate with filesystem-level compromise indicators (unauthorized file access, symbolic link creation).

suggestion.title: FortiOS — Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for the persistence layer that enables continued exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for unexpected symbolic link creation in critical directories (web root, config, library paths). Baseline legitimate symlinks and alert on new creations coinciding with HTTP exploitation patterns or prior filesystem compromise events.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and CISA KEV active exploitation status. Pipeline generated zero hunts despite this being canonical internet-exposed asset scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances exposed on internet-facing ports (80, 443, 8080, 10443). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner for CVE-2025-68686 unpatched status. Alert on any hit as KEV implies active exploitation in wild.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the exploitation vector—directly detectable but pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for anomalous HTTP payloads targeting FortiOS endpoints: atypical User-Agent strings, oversized headers, binary/null bytes in request path, POST requests with unexpected content-types. Cross-reference with known CVE-2025-68686 PoC signatures. Key signal: post-compromise attempts to bypass the patch.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Information Exposure on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is explicit: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline generated no detection UC for data access or exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for unusual access patterns on sensitive resources (configuration backups, credential stores, system logs, SSH keys). Flag outbound data transfers with high entropy or unexpected destinations occurring shortly after web request spikes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypass and Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Pipeline failed to generate UC for this post-compromise persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symbolic link creation/modification attempts, particularly targeting directories that would survive patching. Alert on failed patch integrity checks or rollback attempts. Flag access to symlink targets outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker needs to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' — requires first knowing which FortiOS instances exist and whether they are patched. 'Remote unauthenticated attacker' implies network exposure. No baseline asset hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Fortinet FortiOS instances in the environment via scanner (e.g., Shodan, Censys, or internal asset tools). Cross-reference against patch level for CVE-2025-68686. Flag any instance not patched by federal due date 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Monitoring in FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and mentions vendor patch for it. Pipeline omitted detection for the persistence layer despite clear description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symbolic link creation in system directories (especially those tied to auto-start mechanisms, web server roots, or daemon config paths). Alert on ln -s or equivalent symlink operations outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline failed to propose detection for the exploitation vector post-patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP request logs for anomalous patterns: oversized headers, null-byte injection, path traversal sequences, or unusual parameter encodings targeting known symbolic-link-related endpoints. Correlation with patch-bypass PoC signatures (if available) increases fidelity.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes outcome as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' but pipeline generated no detection for the data collection or exfiltration phase after attacker gains filesystem access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise (after initial CVE exploitation), monitor FortiOS for abnormal file or log access: read operations on /proc, /sys, configuration backups, credential stores, or syslog archives by non-standard processes. Volume-based detection on config file exports.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes active exploitation in CISA KEV. Pipeline must surface detection for the specific CVE attack signature, not just the persistence mechanism that follows. No signature-based IDS/IPS rule suggestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy IDS/IPS signatures detecting exploitation of CVE-2025-68686 (consult Fortinet advisories and public PoCs for payload patterns). Monitor for HTTP 500 errors, memory corruption indicators, or abnormal process spawns immediately after suspicious FortiOS requests.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerability Scanner Hit (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE matching; pipeline generated zero use cases despite article directing readers to substitute 'CVE-2025-68686' into detection templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Fortinet FortiOS assets flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 in your vulnerability scanner. Cross-reference against patch dates to identify lag. Focus on internet-facing FortiGate instances.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'via crafted HTTP requests' — this attack vector requires HTTP-level detection but pipeline produced no network-based use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS HTTP logs for non-standard request patterns that attempt to trigger the CVE-2025-68686 exposure mechanism. Baseline normal admin/API request patterns and alert on deviations sent to known-vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Symbolic Link Filesystem Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — this persistence technique requires filesystem monitoring but was not synthesized into a detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS filesystem for symbolic link creation/modification in configuration, binary, or persistence directories. Focus on symlinks pointing outside expected application directories, suggesting evasion of patch mechanisms or privilege-escalation preparation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Fortinet FortiOS Filesystem Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — this prerequisite requires detection of filesystem-level access/modification but pipeline generated zero file-system-focused use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect evidence of prior successful exploitation (filesystem artifacts, unexpected process spawning, permission changes) on Fortinet FortiOS hosts. Look for artifacts of exploitation frameworks, unusual binary modifications, or unauthorized service startup.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' via bypass of symlink patch — detections should focus on what exfiltration indicators appear after successful exploit, but pipeline produced no post-compromise use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for exfiltration of Fortinet FortiOS configuration files, credential stores, or administrative logs. Correlate with failed/successful FortiGate authentications, unusual administrative access, and outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers bypass the patch 'via crafted HTTP requests.' T1190 applies—remote unauthenticated exploitation against exposed FortiOS appliances. Detection should trigger on HTTP patterns consistent with patch-bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliances for HTTP requests with unusual parameter patterns, request sizes, or header manipulation post-patch. Cross-reference against observed CVE-2025-68686 exploit PoCs. Alert on unauthenticated access to vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—this is the original persistence vector the attacker aims to maintain despite Fortinet's patch. T1547 applies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for symbolic link creation or modification in FortiOS directories, particularly in web-facing or configuration paths. Correlate timing with known compromise indicators or CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Post-exploitation information disclosure must be detected. T1005, T1041 apply.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FortiOS information access patterns (config exports, log reads, credential stores). Alert on anomalous access post-compromise indicators or correlated with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation window.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attackers specifically target the published patch: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' T1036 (obfuscation) or T1562 (modify/disable logging) may apply; look for evidence of patch verification failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FortiOS systems where the published patch (for CVE-2025-68686 / symbolic link fix) is reported as installed but exploitation indicators still fire. Detect patch verification bypass or logging suppression.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' exploits the vulnerability 'via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the primary attack vector and must be detected before successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin/API endpoints for HTTP requests with unusual morphology (oversized headers, polyglot payloads, abnormal URI encoding, or unexpected verbs). Correlate with requests from external IPs and lack of authentication headers. Baseline normal FortiOS traffic first.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Creation on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' established during initial compromise. Filesystem-level monitoring for symlink creation in critical FortiOS paths is essential for detecting post-breach persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ln -s or symlink() creation in FortiOS system directories (/etc/init.d, /bin, config directories, /var/lib). Correlate with unexpected process ownership or system binary modifications. Look for symlinks targeting world-writable paths.

suggestion.title: Post-Patch CVE Bypass Attempts (Installed Patch + Continued Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This indicates patch-evasion behavior—either reusing old symlinks after vendor patch or timing exploitation between patch windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests matching CVE-2025-68686 attack signature on FortiOS instances with vendor patches already deployed (version check via banner grab or scanner integration). Correlated HTTP 401/403 followed by successful auth suggests bypass in progress.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to FortiOS Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' can reach restricted functions. Authentication bypass via crafted HTTP is the entry vector into protected admin panels and APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS admin panels that lack expected authentication tokens (missing session cookies, auth headers, or JWT). Alert on direct access to /admin, /api, /gui paths without prior successful login. Establish baseline by role/source.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [..._TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]' with explicit instruction to substitute CVE-2025-68686. Pipeline should have generated this detection rule immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and patch-management systems for FortiOS appliances missing patches for CVE-2025-68686. Verify patch dates against federal due-date 2026-08-10. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm current deployment status.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the symbolic-link patch. This is the direct exploitation vector and requires HTTP/web-log detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to known Fortinet management ports (443, 8443, 10000) for malformed, oversized, or path-traversal HTTP requests. Flag requests with unusual payloads targeting admin interfaces or symbolic-link-related paths.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence technique being exploited. Must detect symlink creation in FortiOS directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for filesystem events indicating symlink creation or modification in FortiOS installation directories, binary paths, or startup locations. Correlate with process execution events showing malicious binaries being invoked via symlinks.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage FortiOS Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes sequential attack: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' then exploits CVE-2025-68686. Requires correlation of prior-compromise signals with this CVE's exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate indicators of prior FortiOS compromise (unexpected process spawning, filesystem modification, privilege escalation) with subsequent crafted HTTP requests or symlink artifacts. Multi-indicator correlation improves signal-to-noise.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Against Federal Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and states 'patch lag is the silent killer' — requires ongoing compliance monitoring tied to regulatory deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliance inventory for patch compliance status against CVE-2025-68686. Create alerting for any systems still vulnerable after 2026-08-10 deadline. Correlate patch status with network exposure (internal vs. internet-facing).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exposure via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' and mentions 'crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated no use case for detecting this information exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for unusual HTTP request patterns that bypass normal authentication controls. Track outbound data flows from compromised FortiOS appliances to external IPs, focusing on high-volume or suspicious content types. Correlate with filesystem-level compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Bypass on Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and a patch developed to prevent it. No use case captures detection of this persistence technique on the filesystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious symbolic links or symlink creation attempts in FortiOS directories, especially those pointing to sensitive system or configuration paths. Monitor for filesystem activity that recreates symlinks previously patched, indicating bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation: Initial FortiOS Compromise Followed by CVE-2025-68686 Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline missed the chained-attack scenario and the requirement to detect the initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish correlated detections: flag any FortiOS instance showing signs of exploitation of another CVE, followed within days by crafted HTTP requests or filesystem modifications. Prioritize instances in CISA KEV for patch status and active exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Authentication Bypass Detection (CVE-2025-24472)
suggestion.rationale: Article title references CVE-2025-24472 as an authentication bypass in FortiOS and FortiProxy, but the body discussion focuses on CVE-2025-68686. If both CVEs are in scope, the authentication-bypass attack surface requires separate detection logic not present in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication failures followed by successful access without corresponding valid credentials, or for HTTP requests that bypass the normal login flow. Cross-reference with threat intelligence on CVE-2025-24472 exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Relocation to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes core attack: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' This obfuscation enabled the attack but generated no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub release tags for unexpected relocations to commits not on main branches. Alert when semantic version tags (v*) reassign to orphaned commits or commits authored by unusual service accounts. Correlate tag-move events with repository write access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets in GitHub Actions Workflow Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core impact stated: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs…could lead to a devastating breach.' This is the primary harm indicator but no use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching common secret formats (AWS key prefixes, GitHub token patterns, API keys). Alert when repository-configured secrets appear in plaintext output, especially correlating with recent Action repository changes or external dependencies.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise of High-Dependency GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes scale and mechanism: 'About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action' and 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Textbook T1195.003 with zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions and CI/CD platforms for unexpected code changes in repositories with >1000 public dependents. Alert on commit pattern anomalies, external network calls from newly modified Actions, or version tag rewrites that deviate from established release cadence.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Calls from CI/CD Runners
suggestion.rationale: Article notes detection vector: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Detection mechanism identified but not translated to use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS outbound requests from GitHub Actions runner IP ranges to non-standard ports, newly registered domains, or IPs hosting malware. Correlate with recent modifications to the Action repository or newly introduced remote code fetch steps.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Write Access Grants on High-Risk Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Write access was the enabling factor; pre-compromise detection of access anomalies is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub organization audit logs for unexpected collaborator additions or permission escalations on repositories with high external dependents. Alert on write access grants to service accounts with no historical access pattern, external identities, or during non-business hours.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commits with Release Tags
suggestion.rationale: Article devotes extended explanation to this evasion technique: 'Create a branch and push it up to GitHub…Then, delete the remote branch…orphaned commits…are one of the key enabling factors.' Orphaned commits bypassing typical branch-based monitoring should be a detectable pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query GitHub repositories for commits tagged with version strings (v*) but unreachable from any branch. Examine commit content for indicators of malicious payload (subprocess execution, credential handling, external calls). Prioritize repositories with high external dependency counts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Asset Enumeration & Patch-Status Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Fortinet FortiOS as vulnerable product with federal patch due 2026-08-10. Pipeline extracted zero asset-identification queries. Phrase: 'Vendor: Fortinet, Product: FortiOS. Federal patch due: 2026-08-10.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Fortinet FortiOS instances by asset inventory. Cross-reference installed versions against CVE-2025-68686 patch advisory to identify patch lag. Triage unpatched instances by network exposure (internet-facing, DMZ, VPN access).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence File-System Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'establish symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is T1574.004; pipeline extracted zero persistence-artifact detection logic. Phrase: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system for symlink() syscalls, ln -s commands, or unlinkat() operations in privileged/system directories. Correlate symlink creation with suspicious process parents or scheduled tasks. Post-exploitation symlinks often chain privilege escalation or defense evasion.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack mechanism as 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patch. Pipeline extracted zero HTTP exploitation indicators or traffic anomaly detections. Phrase: 'via crafted HTTP requests'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS management/REST APIs with non-standard headers, Content-Length mismatches, encoded payloads, or request patterns that trigger 500-series errors followed by privilege escalation. Correlate with prior symlink filesystem events.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Read & Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is titled 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Article implies attacker reads system config, credentials, logs post-persistence. Pipeline generated zero collection/exfiltration hunts. Phrase: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for reads of sensitive FortiOS files (config, certificate stores, logs, /etc/passwd) from non-privileged or unusual process contexts. Correlate file reads with subsequent DNS lookups or outbound TLS/SSH to external IPs. Watch for file encoding (tar, base64, gzip) as prelude to exfil.

suggestion.title: Prerequisite Vulnerability Exploitation Hunting (Retroactive)
suggestion.rationale: Article requires prior compromise: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline generated zero hunts for the initial foothold. Phrase: 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Retroactively hunt 90-day window prior to any symlink or exfil detection for exploitation attempts against FortiOS: HTTP 400/403 sequences, process crashes, memory faults, or kernel errors. Establish baseline attack that enabled post-compromise persistence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline failed to generate detection logic for the HTTP exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for requests matching known malicious patterns (detailed in Fortinet advisories post-patch). Look for 400-500 series responses or unusual parameter combinations targeting admin/configuration endpoints. Correlate with unauthenticated source IPs.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Creation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence vector. Pipeline failed to capture this technique or generate file-system detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of symbolic links in FortiOS critical directories (e.g., /etc, startup scripts, web roots). Alert on links pointing outside normal application paths or to world-writable locations. Cross-correlate with HTTP exploitation attempts on the same host within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration via FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline should detect unauthorized access to credential storage, config files, or encryption keys post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS configuration and credential storage for unauthorized reads by non-admin processes or from unexpected code paths. Flag access to /etc/passwd equivalents, VPN credential stores, or SSL/TLS keys. Combine with HTTP exploitation signatures for high confidence.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Federal remediation deadline is 2026-08-10; standard asset-exposure hunt applies. Pipeline referenced template but generated no use case covering scanning/inventory for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2025-68686 against all Fortinet FortiOS instances. Flag any device with vulnerability status 'Unpatched' or 'Vulnerable' and escalate to patch management. Cross-reference against network segmentation to identify internet-exposed FortiOS appliances.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Bypass of Symbolic Link Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Detection must distinguish patched vs. unpatched behavior; exploiting a *bypassed* patch implies attackers re-verify persistence after initial patch attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After patch deployment, continue monitoring symbolic link creation even on patched versions. If seen, indicates attacker using known bypass. Alert if symlink attempts correlate with web requests matching CVE-2025-68686 exploitation patterns on systems reporting patch status 'Applied'.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Fortinet FortiOS Unpatched Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' with CVE-2025-68686 as primary IOC. Federal patch due-date is 2026-08-10. Pipeline generated zero inventory-based detections despite this being the canonical CISA KEV hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Fortinet FortiOS appliances in estate with inventory version dates pre-2026-08-10. Cross-reference against CVE-2025-68686 vulnerability scanner results. Flag any unpatched instances in externally-accessible network roles (DMZ, edge, HA clusters) as tier-1 remediation priority.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation of Fortinet FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Pipeline missed this exploitation mechanics entirely—essential for detecting active in-the-wild attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ingress HTTP traffic to Fortinet FortiOS administrative interfaces for payloads containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, encoded variants) or symbolic-link directives. Correlate with POST requests to config-related endpoints. Alert on anomalous HTTP methods or Content-Type mismatches.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise Prerequisite Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline omitted the two-stage attack model entirely; initial compromise detection is critical for preventing cascade exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Fortinet FortiOS systems for unauthorized filesystem write events in critical paths (/bin, /etc, /lib, config directories). Correlate with unexpected process execution, permission changes, or out-of-band authentication attempts. Flag any activity predating HTTP exploitation attempts by hours/days.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Mechanism Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline categorized only T1190; missed T1036/T1027 defense-evasion and persistence phases entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symlink creation, replacement, or modification on Fortinet FortiOS appliances—especially targeting application binaries, library paths, or config directories. Correlate timing with HTTP exploitation logs. Alert on attempts to point symlinks to world-writable or attacker-controlled paths.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Pipeline generated zero detection logic for data theft or unauthorized access to credentials, configs, or logs resulting from CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for bulk reads of sensitive files post-exploitation (system.conf, .ssh directories, syslog archives). Monitor for high-volume data transfers from FortiOS appliances to external IPs. Correlate config-file access with outbound DNS/HTTP queries for data exfil indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Detection (FortiOS Vulnerability Scanner)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2025-68686 as the active KEV. No detection use case was generated despite this being the primary artifact and federal due-date enforcement point (2026-08-10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS instances returning CVE-2025-68686 in vulnerability scans. Prioritize systems on untrusted networks. Cross-reference patch dates against asset inventory; escalate any system not patched by 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Exposed FortiOS Web Interface on Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can exploit via 'crafted HTTP requests', establishing public-facing web exposure as the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS admin/management ports (443, 8443) answering from internet sources. Correlate network exposure with unpatched asset status. Flag if certificate metadata or HTTP fingerprints match known FortiOS patterns on public IPs.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases', establishing filesystem persistence as second-stage technique after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation in FortiOS-owned directories (/etc, /var/www, /etc/init.d). Flag attempts to link critical boot/startup scripts. Cross-reference with file integrity monitoring to detect post-exploitation filesystem manipulation.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Patch Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism... via crafted HTTP requests', indicating defense-evasion via malformed payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests with suspicious encoding (double-encoding, null bytes, unicode escapes), oversized payloads, malformed headers, or path-traversal patterns sent to FortiOS endpoints. Correlate with CVE-2025-68686 scanner results to enrich context.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Post-Exploitation Filesystem Access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level', indicating pre-requisite filesystem-level breach enabling symlink placement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-administrative processes accessing critical FortiOS directories. Correlate with prior successful CVE exploitation attempts or credential compromise indicators to identify attack chain from initial breach through persistence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patch and exploit symbolic link persistency. No detection hypothesis generated for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for HTTP requests containing unusual parameter combinations, unexpected header patterns, or request sizes that deviate from normal baseline traffic. Correlate with post-authentication events and filesystem access to identify patch-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Monitoring on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a core persistence technique and should trigger filesystem monitoring use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation or manipulation in FortiOS configuration directories, especially those pointing to web-accessible paths or system binaries. Cross-reference with HTTP request patterns for post-compromise initialization.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance and Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes patch bypass as attack method ('bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'). Patch compliance and post-patch exploitation should be tracked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline all FortiOS instances for patch level against August 10, 2026 due date. Flag any instances showing HTTP activity consistent with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation (crafted requests) despite patch version claims, indicating bypass or scanner evasion.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Information Disclosure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is classified as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Detection should focus on data exfiltration post-compromise, not just the exploit mechanics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data volumes leaving FortiOS systems post-exploitation. Track access to sensitive configuration files (certificates, authentication tokens, routing tables) by unauthorized processes or via unusual HTTP methods.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise Indicators Leading to FortiOS Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite access is part of the kill chain but generates no detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem write events to FortiOS binary/config directories with subsequent HTTP request anomalies. Flag any instances showing filesystem-level tampering (permission changes, file writes) preceding the crafted HTTP requests described in the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes attack surface: 'remote unauthenticated attacker' + 'FortiOS' implies public-facing instances are primary target. Pipeline omitted baseline asset detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances with public IP assignment or internet-facing DNS records. Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to establish baseline of exposed instances and version inventory.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'patch developed for symbolic link persistency' and federal patch due date 2026-08-10; pipeline failed to generate patch detection. Critical for breach prevention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanners for FortiOS instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 (unpatched versions). Flag any exposed instance as critical priority given CISA KEV status and active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to FortiOS Admin Console
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'via crafted HTTP requests' targeting already-compromised instances. Pipeline missed exploit detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin endpoints (443, 8443) for malformed headers, suspicious User-Agent strings, or request patterns consistent with bypass attempts against patch-mitigation logic. Baseline legitimate admin access and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Symbolic Link Modification on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'; pipeline omitted persistence detection related to the specific vulnerability mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for symbolic link creation or modification on compromised FortiOS systems at filesystem level, particularly in web-root or config directories. Cross-correlate with HTTP request logs to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'; pipeline generated no post-compromise hunting logic for data access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For FortiOS instances previously identified as compromised or with indicators of exploit, hunt for unusual access to configuration files, credential stores, or sensitive logs (e.g., admin credentials, VPN user databases, firewall rules).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker must first 'have compromised the product via another vulnerability' and then escalate; pipeline omitted detection for secondary compromise attempts originating from FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections originating from known-compromised FortiOS instances to internal resources (SMB, RDP, SSH, WinRM). Establish baseline of legitimate management traffic and escalate deviations, especially outbound from admin VLANs.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers exploit 'public-facing application' and CISA KEV implies active scanning. Detection should identify FortiOS assets accessible from untrusted networks via network scanning or configuration review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances responding to HTTP requests from external sources. Look for HTTP User-Agent patterns typical of FortiOS or known scanner signatures attempting to fingerprint the product.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers bypass the patch 'via crafted HTTP requests.' Detection should capture malformed or anomalous HTTP request patterns targeting FortiOS services post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for FortiOS endpoints showing unusual request patterns: non-standard HTTP methods, oversized headers, special characters in URL paths, or Content-Type mismatches. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or suspicious parameter values.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'bypass' of that mechanism, indicating attacker creates or manipulates symbolic links post-compromise. Detection should alert on filesystem operations related to symlink creation in critical directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for symlink creation or traversal attempts in FortiOS configuration or binary directories. Look for processes spawned by admin or system accounts that reference /proc/self/fd or similar symlink paths, and cross-reference with post-exploitation timeframes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Vulnerability Confirmation Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article implies patched versions exist. Detection should confirm whether endpoints have been patched or remain vulnerable by querying vulnerability scanner data or native FortiOS version enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match FortiOS product inventory against CVE-2025-68686 patch baseline. Flag any instances running versions known to be vulnerable or with patch date before federal due date 2026-08-10. Cross-correlate with network segmentation rules.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit HTTP Admin API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker must first compromise FortiOS 'via another vulnerability' then bypass patch via HTTP. Detection should identify anomalous admin API calls post-initial-compromise, such as credential changes, policy modifications, or data exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS admin console (/admin, /api/v2/cmdb) from non-approved source IPs, especially those without valid session cookies or with reused tokens. Correlate with successful authentication only to admin accounts, and look for config modification events immediately after.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism ... via crafted HTTP requests' but pipeline provides no HTTP-level detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS web interfaces (ports 80, 443, 10000, 8443) for HTTP requests with suspicious or malformed parameters consistent with patch-bypass attempts. Correlate against device version to identify unpatched instances. Flag requests deviating from normal administrative traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Patch Compliance and Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10 for compliance audits, but pipeline provides no asset-inventory or patch-status use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability-management and CMDB systems for Fortinet FortiOS instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Flag instances in internet-exposed or DMZ segments. Alert on instances not patched by 2026-08-10 federal due date to support regulatory compliance workflows.

suggestion.title: Symbolic-Link Persistence Detection on Fortinet Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and notes 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — establishing post-exploitation persistence requirement absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem logs and file-integrity systems for creation of symbolic links in web-accessible directories (/var/www, /usr/local/share/fortiweb) pointing to config or credential storage. Alert on link creation outside normal administrative hours or by non-privileged processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Extraction of FortiOS Sensitive Information Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor' but pipeline contains no detection for unauthorized config access, credential theft, or exfiltration following compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk extraction of FortiOS administrative credentials, VPN configurations, firewall rule sets, or system logs following filesystem-level compromise indicators. Monitor for subsequent anomalous outbound connections over non-standard ports from affected device IP space.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt — Anomalous HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector and that exploits target FortiOS admin interfaces. Pipeline generated zero use cases for this explicit attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS /admin, /api/, and /cgi-bin endpoints for POST/PUT requests with unusual payloads (e.g., path traversal patterns, symbolic link references, or requests from non-standard User-Agents). Flag patterns matching known FortiOS exploitation frameworks targeting this CVE.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistency — Post-Exploitation Filesystem Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' but no detection for symbolic link creation or filesystem persistence was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links pointing to FortiOS system directories (/etc, /root, /usr/bin) or temporary paths. Correlate with prior CVE-2025-68686 exploitation indicators to confirm post-compromise persistence setup.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Information Disclosure — Sensitive Config File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'may allow...bypass...unauthorized actor' to access sensitive info; impact is information disclosure but no detection for reading protected config or credential files was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for read access to sensitive paths (e.g., /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow variants, FortiOS config backups, VPN credential stores) following anomalous HTTP activity. Flag processes spawned by web services (fortishell, httpd) reading files outside normal operational scope.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthenticated Remote Access — Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and bypass of existing security controls; no detection rule for authentication-bypass patterns generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiOS admin endpoints with missing or malformed authentication headers, or requests that succeed despite 401/403 responses to prior requests from same source. Track bypass success rates by source IP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Prerequisite Compromise — Multi-Stage Attack Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' No correlation rule for detecting this prerequisite initial compromise was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of FortiOS vulnerability scans flagging other pre-2025-68686 CVEs. Create hunt for systems with active exploitation indicators (failed RCE attempts, webshell paths) followed within 48h by 2025-68686-specific HTTP patterns; indicates staged attack.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Status Verification — Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article notes federal due date 2026-08-10 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'; no use case for identifying unpatched FortiOS versions in fleet inventory was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset inventory for FortiOS instances with versions < fixed build (requires Fortinet advisory for exact version ranges). Cross-reference with network telemetry to identify which systems accept inbound HTTP/S on admin ports; prioritize remediation for internet-facing assets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2025-68686 as the actively exploited CVE with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10. Pipeline must detect vulnerable FortiOS versions via scanner fingerprint, HTTP header disclosure, or patch-status cross-check against asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances running vulnerable versions via vulnerability scanner exports or HTTP responses disclosing version strings. Cross-reference asset inventory to flag systems not remediated by 2026-08-10 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Attackers create symlinks in FortiOS filesystem to maintain foothold after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symlink creation (ln -s calls) in FortiOS protected directories (/usr/local/fortisandbox, /etc/fortigate, /var/cache/forticlient). Flag symlinks pointing to writable temp directories or scripts. Monitor for post-exploit symlink overwrites of system binaries.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass HTTP Request Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism via crafted HTTP requests.' Must detect polymorph requests circumventing input validation patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed HTTP requests to known-vulnerable FortiOS endpoints (e.g., /upload, /api, /admin) with special character encoding, multi-stage payloads, or boundary-bypass patterns. Correlate with POST/GET responses indicating patch-bypass success (symlink creation side-effects, file disclosure).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' exploiting 'public-facing application.' Must detect unauthorized access to FortiOS management interfaces without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to FortiOS admin/API endpoints (ports 80, 443, 8080, 10443) from external IPs returning 401/403 authentication failures. Flag sequences of requests probing multiple endpoints without auth headers or with invalid tokens pre-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information' after 'prior filesystem level' compromise. Detect abnormal access to configuration, credential, or API-key files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads on sensitive FortiOS config paths (/etc/fortiweb.conf, /etc/fortisandbox.conf, /etc/passwd, /var/log/authlog) from unexpected processes or UIDs. Correlate with prior symlink-creation or patch-bypass signals. Flag exfiltration attempts (curl/wget) of config file contents.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Privilege Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level,' indicating lateral privilege escalation from restricted process context to system/root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process fork/exec sequences escalating from sandboxed FortiOS services (fortisandbox, fortiweb daemons) to root-level actions. Flag access to /proc/*/mem, ptrace calls, or kernel module loading from unprivileged contexts. Monitor setuid/setgid bit abuse on FortiOS binaries.

suggestion.title: Compromised NPM Package Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states @joyfill/components and @joyfill/layouts are compromised; no use case for detecting installation of known-bad npm packages in package.lock or npm install logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn install, and pnpm install processes for package manager invocations installing @joyfill/components or @joyfill/layouts. Cross-reference against threat feed of compromised package names and versions. Flag installations on development and CI/CD systems.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Execution from Node Modules
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Obfuscated Remote Access Trojan'; pipeline missed T1027 defense-evasion indicator for obfuscated payloads embedded in node_modules during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.js or JavaScript engine executing heavily obfuscated code from node_modules directory. Look for suspicious eval(), Function constructor, or atob() chains originating from installed dependencies. Flag high entropy strings being decoded at runtime.

suggestion.title: RAT Command & Control Communication from Application Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RAT payload; no detection for outbound C2 communication initiated by Node.js or application processes loading compromised npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound HTTPS or DNS queries from node.js processes against known RAT C2 infrastructure. Monitor for long-lived connections or periodic beaconing patterns from application entry-points that depend on @joyfill packages.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from Node.js
suggestion.rationale: RAT typically requires code execution and reverse shell capability; no use case for detecting shell spawning from npm-installed code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.js or npm processes spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh with command-line arguments. Correlate parent process tree to installed packages. Flag child_process module calls with network-suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Package Lock File Modification Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often alter lock files to persist across dependency updates; no detection for tampering with package-lock.json or yarn.lock after initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-lock.json and yarn.lock for suspicious hash mismatches or version downgrades matching known-compromised package releases. Detect modifications to lock files immediately following npm install or package manager invocations.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via Obfuscated Dependency Payloads
suggestion.rationale: RAT payloads typically enumerate system info and running processes; no detection for discovery commands embedded or scheduled via npm post-install scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag post-install scripts or require-time code execution that invokes system discovery commands (whoami, hostname, netstat, tasklist, ps, etc.) without legitimate build-time justification. Correlate with @joyfill package installation.

suggestion.title: ClickHouse database error logs from malformed/injected SQL
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers inject 'arbitrary SQL by using trailing backslash'—successful injection will either execute or generate database errors. Pipeline missed application/database log detection. Article phrase: 'allows arbitrary SQL execution' implies backend logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query ClickHouse system.query_log for syntax errors or unexpected query patterns (e.g., UNION, OR 1=1) originating from HTTP requests. Correlate with escapeValue() stack traces or process memory analysis showing backslash bypass logic triggered. High-confidence signal if error occurs immediately after HTTP request containing backslash-quote in parameter.

suggestion.title: @hypequery/clickhouse process communication anomaly detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes escapeValue() function vulnerability—monitoring the vulnerable library's function calls or memory behavior during exploitation would detect injection in-flight. Missing: dynamic analysis of the vulnerable code path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process executing @hypequery/clickhouse or Node.js with embedded hypequery when receiving HTTP requests with backslash-quote patterns in parameters, followed by unexpected child processes (sqlclient, curl to external IPs, base64 encoding tools) or high volume of database queries in short window. Correlate HTTP request timestamp with process execution within 100ms.

suggestion.title: Version mismatch: @hypequery/clickhouse <2.0.2 still running post-patching
suggestion.rationale: Patch available (2.0.2+), but article states 'versions prior to 2.0.2 who pass user-controlled input'—many orgs delay patching. Missing: detection for unpatched systems still in production after advisory release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package manager logs or process execution for @hypequery/clickhouse binary/module load with version <2.0.2 post-2026-07-28 (advisory date). Cross-reference against patch deployment logs. Flag if system is internet-facing (has public DNS, listening on 0.0.0.0, exposed via CDN/LB).

suggestion.title: POST-exploitation: data exfiltration via SQLi result tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'allows arbitrary SQL execution' but provides no hunts for successful exploitation outcomes. Attacker would exfiltrate data via injected SELECT statements tunneled through HTTP response or error messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP responses >10KB or unusual Content-Type (application/octet-stream from JSON API) correlating with database query errors or long query execution time. Detect SELECT INTO OUTFILE patterns in HTTP requests or error messages. Flag if response contains CSV/JSON data structure matching database schema.

suggestion.title: WAF/IDS bypass indicators: double-encoding and normalization evasion
suggestion.rationale: The pipeline's UC_2_2 assumes URL encoding consistency, but sophisticated attackers will use double-encoding (%255c), mixed case (%5C vs %5c), or unicode normalization to bypass pattern matching. Article doesn't mention evasion, but a critical SQL injection warrants it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed HTTP requests (403/406 from WAF) to same endpoint followed by successful request (200) with different parameter encoding. Flag if single source cycles through >5 different encoding variants of backslash-quote pattern within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable @hypequery/clickhouse dependency in npm shrinkwrap/package-lock.json
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies package & version; runtime detection only catches active exploitation. Missing: pre-deployment/build-time detection of vulnerable dependency in source code repositories and artifact repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package-lock.json / yarn.lock / shrinkwrap.json in all code repos and CI/CD artifact repos for @hypequery/clickhouse version <2.0.2. Alert on pull requests adding or keeping the vulnerable version post-2026-07-28. Cross-ref against deploy logs to identify running instances.

suggestion.title: WebDAV MOVE with Overwrite:T header targeting existing file
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states MOVE with 'Overwrite: T' performs explicit RemoveAll on destination—this header presence is the attack signature. Searching for MOVE requests carrying Overwrite: True against existing destination paths is precise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebDAV MOVE/COPY requests with Overwrite: True header sent against a goshs server (identify via banner or HTTP Server header). Correlate with file access logs to confirm destination existed pre-request and was deleted/overwritten post-request.

suggestion.title: goshs version running without patch for CVE-2026-64863 or CVE-2026-50138
suggestion.rationale: Article references two CVEs, indicating this is a known vulnerability with a patch. Detection should identify goshs versions vulnerable to this bypass, not just --no-delete flag presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify goshs process with version < [fixed version] running with --no-delete flag. Query against process inventory or EDR Process telemetry for Version field. A baseline should include goshs binaries with hash signatures of vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Destination header rewrite in WebDAV MOVE to exfiltrate/modify unintended files
suggestion.rationale: WebDAV MOVE allows specifying a Destination header distinct from the path being moved. Article describes 'MOVE deletes source file...and with Overwrite: T it additionally performs RemoveAll on destination'—an attacker could exploit this to delete files outside their intended scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all WebDAV MOVE/COPY requests and compare the request path with the Destination header value. Flag when Destination points to a different directory or filename than the request path, especially if the destination previously existed (check access logs for pre-move activity).

suggestion.title: goshs listening on web port without authentication + --no-delete but accepting MOVE
suggestion.rationale: Article describes running with '--w --no-delete' (likely -w for web mode). Lack of authentication coupled with disabled DELETE but enabled MOVE creates the bypass condition. Detection should identify this configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify goshs processes listening on HTTP/HTTPS (port 80, 443, or common alternate web ports) with --no-delete flag in command line AND WebDAV protocol active (detect via OPTIONS request support or presence of WebDAV-specific headers in responses).

suggestion.title: Source file present before WebDAV MOVE, absent after (file deletion via protocol)
suggestion.rationale: The attack succeeds when MOVE destroys the source file while --no-delete is supposed to prevent it. A precise signature is: file enumeration shows file exists, WebDAV MOVE succeeds, file no longer exists at original path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WebDAV access logs (MOVE/COPY requests) with file system audit logs or directory listing snapshots. Flag when a MOVE request succeeds (201/204) but the source path no longer contains the file immediately after (requires file listing or audit log confirmation of deletion).

suggestion.title: goshs process spawned with -sftp and -b flags simultaneously
suggestion.rationale: The article emphasizes the combination of `-sftp` and `-b 'admin:'` in a single invocation. A process-creation detection that correlates both flags on the same cmdline strengthens initial-access detection. Article: 'Start goshs v2.1.3 with `-b 'admin:' -sftp`. No `-fkf`.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation of goshs/goshs.exe where the command line contains both `-sftp` and `-b` flags in sequence, indicating SFTP listener with basic authentication enabled. Exclude processes with `-fkf` flag (the published fix). This is the tell-tale sign of vulnerable configuration.

suggestion.title: Comparison of goshs instances with and without -fkf flag presence
suggestion.rationale: The article explicitly states that CVE-2026-40884 was incompletely fixed and that adding `-fkf` is the mitigation. A compliance-style hunt should track which goshs processes lack this protective flag. Article: 'CVE-2026-40884 blocks the empty-username variant... The empty-password variant bypasses that fix.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all goshs/goshs.exe process invocations across the estate. Flag any that include `-sftp` and `-b` but LACK the `-fkf` flag. This identifies unpatched/misconfigured listeners vulnerable to CVE-2026-62325 and the prior CVE-2026-40884.

suggestion.title: Credential submission to SFTP listener (empty-password or empty-username auth attempts)
suggestion.rationale: If SFTP auth logs or SSH logs capture the actual authentication exchange, empty-password or empty-username login attempts (via SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST or similar) to port 2121 would be direct evidence of exploitation. Article narrative: 'SFTP accepts connections without password' and 'empty-password variant'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt SSH/SFTP protocol-level auth attempts where username field is populated but password field is empty, or vice versa. Focus on connections to goshs listener ports (2121 if default). This may require SSH daemon or SFTP client logs on the network segment.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Vulnerable Endpoints

Focus on requests arriving at unpatched FortiOS instances within your environment.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Persistence and Symlink Traversal Attempts
