Symlink traversal attempts (reading/writing outside intended directories) are a key bypass indicator for the patched vulnerability.

suggestion.title: FortiOS System Information Discovery Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Following initial filesystem compromise, attacker will enumerate system state; article describes prior compromise scenario requiring discovery of vulnerable FortiOS instance state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance queries on compromised FortiOS systems: process enumeration (ps, netstat), network scanning (nmap, curl to local services), and queries to system files (/proc, /etc). These precede the HTTP-based exploitation phase.

suggestion.title: HTTP Status Anomalies and Error Responses from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Crafted HTTP requests targeting the patch bypass will generate atypical responses; article implies requests that evade newly-deployed mitigations.

suggestion.title: Pre-Compromise Vulnerability Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article prerequisite: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'. Initial-access vulnerability must be caught to prevent the CVE-2025-68686 chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS attack and error logs for exploitation signatures of related RCE or memory-corruption vulnerabilities. Monitor for unexpected child processes, privilege escalation events, or filesystem-level modifications suggesting initial compromise occurred.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Patch-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: CVE category is 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'—impact phase includes unauthorized access to confidential data after patch bypass succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS audit logs for unauthorized access to sensitive resources (VPN credentials, certificates, configuration backups, session keys) by unauthenticated or unprivileged accounts. Track unusual data exports, diagnostic bundle downloads, or config access patterns correlating with unpatched scanner status.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 — Crafted HTTP Exploit Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker...via crafted HTTP requests'. Primary attack vector entirely undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor exposed FortiOS instances for HTTP requests with path traversal sequences, symbolic link references, or other malformed payloads from unauthenticated sources. Baseline normal request patterns and alert on deviations matching known bypass techniques for patched symbolic link defenses.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Post-Exploitation Symbolic Link Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'. This defense-evasion persistence technique has no detection hypothesis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation/modification in FortiOS system directories, particularly targeting config or backup paths. Track symlink targets escaping expected directory bounds. Correlate symlink operations with suspicious process execution or prior exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'. No detection for post-exploit data collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized access to FortiOS sensitive files (configuration, credentials, certificates, keys). Flag sequential reads across multiple sensitive locations. Alert on config exports or credential dumps following exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 — Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due 2026-08-10 per article. No inventory-based detection for vulnerability status or remediation drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for FortiOS versions below patched baseline. Baseline scan dates to identify gaps. Alert if vulnerable versions still present post-deadline or if assets show 'last scan unknown'. Cross-reference with firewall rulebase changes suggesting attempted exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Multi-Stage Attack Chain — Initial Filesystem Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'. Two-stage attack requiring detection of initial compromise before CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish filesystem access baseline for FortiOS administrative processes. Flag unauthorized filesystem writes to system directories or kernel/core areas. Alert on privilege escalation attempts or process spawning that precedes HTTP exploitation. Correlate with CVE activity timelines.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV implies active exploitation and mandates federal patching by 2026-08-10; baseline inventory + patch-lag detection mandatory. Article: 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch-management data for FortiOS assets where CVE-2025-68686 remains unpatched or scanner confidence is low. Look for systems reporting product=FortiOS where patch_date > 2026-08-10 or patch_date is null. Correlate with asset exposure tools (Shodan, Censys) to identify internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence on FortiOS Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'; detection needed to spot already-compromised FortiOS systems. Article phrase: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem events for suspicious symbolic link creation in configuration or web-root directories (commonly /etc, /var/www, /data). Look for links created by unprivileged processes or pointing outside expected boundaries. Correlate with evidence of prior file-system access.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Patterns: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism via crafted HTTP requests'; log HTTP access patterns for indicators of exploitation attempts. Article phrase: 'via crafted HTTP requests.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Signature-hunt for HTTP requests targeting FortiOS with unusual parameter encoding, path traversal indicators, or symlink-traversal attempts in request URIs. Look for repeated requests from same source post-patching, suggesting attacker is testing bypass. Flag requests with malformed headers or null-byte injection patterns common in symlink exploits.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is categorized as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'; detection should focus on data exfiltration and unauthorized reads. Article: 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor Vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for reads/downloads of sensitive configuration files (admin credentials, VPN keys, firewall rules, certificates) from unexpected user accounts or IPs. Look for bulk exfiltration patterns in outbound traffic post-compromise (large data volumes to external IPs, encrypted tunnels from FortiOS). Correlate with symbolic-link and HTTP-bypass detections.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes kill-chain: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' then uses CVE-2025-68686 for bypass; requires correlation of initial-access + persistence + evasion signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate three signals within 7-day window on same FortiOS asset: (1) exploit attempt against ANY FortiOS CVE or suspicious shell/file-system access, (2) symbolic link creation in sensitive paths, (3) crafted HTTP requests or patch-bypass indicators. Alert on correlation; lower threshold if asset is internet-facing per asset-exposure hunt.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Prior Compromise via Unknown Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise via 'another vulnerability' is prerequisite; detection should hunt for any FortiOS intrusion indicators pre-dating CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempt. Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Review FortiOS logs (auth, access, file-system, network) for anomalous activity 7+ days before any CVE-2025-68686 exploitation signals. Look for unusual login attempts, unexpected processes, or filesystem modifications that pre-date known compromise indicators. Cross-reference with threat intel on other FortiOS 0-days or recent CVEs.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Asset Vulnerability Scan (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets CVE-2025-68686 as CISA KEV (actively exploited). Baseline detection requires asset inventory + vuln scanner match. 'Remote unauthenticated attacker' via 'crafted HTTP requests' implies scanning infrastructure should flag FortiOS instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management database for FortiOS instances. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2025-68686 status. Alert on unpatched instances with exposure to internet-facing HTTP/HTTPS interfaces. Correlate patch application date against federal due date 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence vector this patch was meant to block. Post-compromise, attacker leverages symlinks for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symlink creation in startup/autorun paths (e.g., /etc/init.d, systemd service paths). Flag symlinks pointing to attacker-controlled locations or unusual ownership. Cross-correlate with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Patch Bypass via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism… via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the active exploitation vector—malformed requests evade patch logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect FortiOS HTTP request logs for malformed or unusual request patterns (missing headers, oversized payloads, control-character injection, path traversal attempts). Correlate with CVE-2025-68686 POC signatures if available. Focus on requests to symlink-related paths or administrative endpoints.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'—the impact of successful exploitation. Post-patch-bypass, attacker gains unauthorized data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS traffic logs for unusual outbound data transfer volume, especially from admin/config directories or credential stores. Flag extraction of sensitive files (configs, logs, certificates). Correlate with filesystem persistence indicators and patch-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Post-Exploit Access on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Implies prior RCE; this detection covers suspicious filesystem activity post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual process spawning or file modification in FortiOS system directories post-compromise (e.g., /opt/lib, /var/lib, startup scripts). Flag privilege escalation attempts, library hijacking via symlinks, or execution of non-standard binaries in trusted paths.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance and Patch-Gap Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article includes federal patch due date (2026-08-10) and emphasizes CISA KEV status. Operational requirement: hunt all FortiOS instances for patch lag, since 'patch lag is the silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Fortinet FortiOS instances for installed patch level vs. CVE-2025-68686 fix. Flag any instance on EOL versions or with >30-day patch lag. Cross-check with federal compliance timeline. Surface instances behind proxies or on isolated segments that may be overlooked.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Scanner Match — FortiOS Info Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2025-68686 and states vulnerability scanner matching is the baseline hunt. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being a CISA KEV (active exploitation) with a federal patch deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any FortiOS asset reporting CVE-2025-68686 as unpatched. Cross-reference against exposure scans to identify public-facing instances. CISA KEV status implies active wild exploitation; even patched systems warrant validation due to patch-lag risk.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS — CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline missed this specific attack vector; HTTP logs are the telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin interfaces (TCP 80, 443, 8443) for anomalous patterns: excessive parameter manipulation, requests targeting filesystem paths (/proc, /dev), or attempts to interact with symbolic link targets. Correlate with baseline FortiOS admin traffic.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Exploitation — Persistency Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the target; this is a Windows/Linux filesystem forensic indicator the pipeline ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for FortiOS process or daemon activity creating or traversing symbolic links in system directories (/etc, /var, /opt/fortinet). Alert on ln -s execution targeting patch files or binaries. Check filesystem event logs for symlink creation post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is named 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'; pipeline created no detection for actual data exfiltration or information exposure events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from FortiOS (after initial compromise) for bulk data transfer, encrypted tunnels, or DNS exfiltration. Alert on unexpected egress to non-administrative destinations. Correlate with vulnerability scanner alerts for this CVE to confirm context.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Privilege Escalation via Filesystem Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—pipeline omitted the two-stage kill chain and filesystem-access indicators entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated filesystem access to FortiOS directories (e.g., /opt/fortinet, /etc/fortios config paths). Alert on privilege escalation attempts following initial compromise. Correlate with web logs showing exploitation of the initial-stage vulnerability that precedes CVE-2025-68686 abuse.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Pointer Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'The attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit'. No use case generated for detecting tag movement to orphaned or unexpected commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on release tags (v*) being moved to commits not reachable from main branch or commits with unusually few parents. Correlate with code review bypass indicators. Look for tags moved to commits authored by non-maintainers.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exposed in GitHub Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs'. Article emphasizes this 'could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public'. No detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for plaintext secret patterns (AWS_SECRET_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, API keys) within 60 seconds of workflow execution. Correlate with recent updates to referenced Action versions or tags.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Referenced in Workflow Definitions
suggestion.rationale: Article details the technique: 'Changing existing release tags to point to the attack commit' where the 'attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch'. Attack succeeded by users unknowingly referencing the orphaned malicious commit via version tags.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference workflow YAML files (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) with the commit graph to detect references (via SHA or tag) to commits not reachable from the default branch. Flag as anomalous if the commit author differs from the Action maintainer list.

suggestion.title: Unexpected External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity'. No detection logic captured for this pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections initiated from GitHub Actions runners (identifiable by runner IP ranges and user-agent) to non-whitelisted external domains. Alert on downloads of executable or script content (curl/wget to unfamiliar hosts) within 5 seconds of Action execution start.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Access by Non-Maintainers or New Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit'. The permission escalation or account compromise enabling this access is a critical detection gap: 'As of this writing, it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions on the repo'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on write access grants to high-dependency repositories (track star count / fork count as proxy). Flag commits to main/release branches authored by accounts with <30 days age or recent permission escalation. Cross-reference with MFA bypass or session anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Version Tag Downgrade or Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Users who explicitly pinned versions (e.g., `tj-actions/changed-files@v35`) would unwittingly pull the malicious version after tag redirection. No detection for when pinned Action versions suddenly execute unexpected code paths or network calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected network destinations and subprocess behaviors for each Action version + tag. Alert when a pinned Action version (e.g., v35) suddenly initiates outbound connections, spawns new processes, or modifies environment variables that differ from historical runs of the same tag.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Inventory and Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and provides template reference; zero use cases generated despite this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiOS instances in environment via port scanning (443/tcp, 8443/tcp for admin interfaces) and check patch status against 2026-08-10 federal due date. Cross-reference asset inventory against vulnerability scanner baseline to identify patch lag.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Attempts to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation vector: 'via crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch' — requires detection for anomalous HTTP payloads targeting FortiOS admin endpoints post-patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to /admin/*, /api/*, or /cgi-bin/* endpoints on FortiOS for payloads with unusual encoding, multipart boundaries, or nested escaping patterns matching symbolic link path traversal indicators mentioned in article.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — requires filesystem monitoring for suspicious symlink creation in FortiOS directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS configuration directories (/etc/*, /var/etc/*, /data/*) pointing outside normal system paths, particularly those created in timeframe matching patch release.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Information Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' — requires detection for unauthorized data reads/exfiltration post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication logs showing successful admin-level access post-patch combined with abnormal file read patterns from /data/config*, /etc/passwd-equivalent, or /data/certs directories followed by outbound HTTPS to non-Fortinet IPs.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise Pre-Cursor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — this two-stage attack requires early detection of filesystem tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful exploitation of pre-exploitation CVEs in FortiOS (search recent CISA KEV entries for Fortinet) combined with filesystem write activity in protected directories within 48 hours prior to HTTP exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states this CISA KEV entry 'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild'—mandatory scanning and inventory control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability management systems for CVE-2025-68686 detection on FortiOS products. Prioritize by federal due date 2026-08-10. Flag any system claiming remediation via patch but still showing vuln status (bypass detection).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Detection (Post-Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence technique being exploited and patched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for unexpected symlink creation in /lib, /bin, or init directories. Cross-reference symlink targets against known-good binaries. Alert on symlinks created post-compromise (correlate with other indicators of filesystem access).

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Patterns Targeting Symlink Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the actual exploitation vector post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints with encoded payloads, null bytes, or path traversal patterns targeting /sys or /lib endpoints. Correlate with recent filesystem modifications or failed authentication attempts immediately preceding exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unauthenticated FortiOS Internet-Facing Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' capability, requiring network exposure to internet or untrusted networks without authentication gateway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiOS management interfaces (443, 8443, 10443) exposed to internet or DMZ without WAF/reverse-proxy authentication. Cross-reference with patch status; flag unpatched instances as critical-severity exposure.

suggestion.title: Prerequisite Filesystem Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—detect the chained-exploitation pattern before symlink persistence is installed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized filesystem modifications in FortiOS (especially /etc, /lib, /bin) occurring before or concurrent with HTTP request anomalies. Correlate file-permission changes or ownership modifications with subsequent exploitation attempts within 24-hour window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation of FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker...via crafted HTTP requests' and implies active exploitation in CISA KEV. Pipeline generated zero use cases for HTTP-based exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiOS web admin interfaces (typical ports 80, 443, 8080) from untrusted sources with suspicious parameter combinations or payloads known to bypass authentication. Flag requests with non-standard User-Agent headers or rapid request sequences within seconds.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exposed Asset Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article's multi-stage attack requires 'first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability,' implying reconnaissance/scanning phase. No use case for detecting FortiOS exposure on public-facing networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect identification of publicly accessible FortiOS instances via characteristic banner-grabbing (HTTP 401 responses with FortiOS headers), Shodan/zoomeye scanning signatures, or TLS certificate queries for 'fortios' or 'fortiweb' FQDN patterns in DNS exfiltration logs.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise Precursor (CVE Unknown)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite stage is entirely unmapped. Pipeline missed the two-stage nature of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliances for file-system write activity in privileged directories (e.g., `/etc`, `/opt/fortinet`, web root paths) from unexpected service accounts or child processes. Cross-reference with CVE databases for known pre-exploitation vulnerabilities affecting FortiOS file-system access.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article's impact is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No use case for detecting post-exploitation data access or exfiltration patterns from FortiOS config/logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large data transfers from FortiOS management interfaces to external IPs immediately following exploitation attempts. Monitor FortiOS log export/backup operations initiated by new or suspicious user accounts. Flag access to sensitive files (VPN configs, admin credentials, policy databases) in FortiOS filesystem.

suggestion.title: Patch-Bypass HTTP Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection logic for malformed/crafted requests designed to evade patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with path traversal sequences (`../`, `..\`, URL encoding variants), double-encoding, null bytes, or symbolic-link references in FortiOS endpoints. Correlate with HTTP responses indicating successful bypass (200 OK post-patch, or access to previously-protected resources).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Vulnerability Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2025-68686 is explicitly named in the article as the actionable indicator for CISA KEV exploitation. Pipeline failed to generate the baseline asset-exposure UC despite article guidance pointing to `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for FortiOS appliances matching CVE-2025-68686 signature or running versions prior to patched release. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed management interfaces, public-facing deployments, or instances not patched by federal due date (2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Bypass Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests' post-compromise. This is a direct exploitation mechanism the pipeline did not capture in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin/API endpoints for bypassing payloads: malformed Content-Length headers, unusual URI encoding, path traversal sequences, or requests that succeed despite prior authentication failures. Correlate with filesystem events showing symlink manipulation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem Symbolic Link Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the method for maintaining post-compromise access. Filesystem monitoring for symlink abuse is a critical detection gap not addressed by any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links within FortiOS system directories (config paths, log directories, startup scripts). Flag symlinks with targets outside expected FortiOS application tree or pointing to sensitive OS paths. Correlate with prior HTTP bypass activity.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Compromise Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability...at filesystem level.' Initial compromise is a distinct stage requiring detection before the HTTP bypass exploit fires.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect first-stage FortiOS compromise: unexpected process execution, memory corruption events, application crashes, file system writes to restricted directories, or sudden elevation of FortiOS service privileges. Flag if followed within hours by HTTP requests with bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability title explicitly includes 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Detection should cover post-exploitation data access, not just the bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FortiOS processes or HTTP sessions reading/transmitting sensitive config files, credential stores, or certificate material after successful bypass exploitation. Alert on unusual data volume egress from FortiOS appliance to external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation of FortiOS Post-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' Core initial exploitation vector. No detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints from unauthenticated sources using obfuscated payloads, path traversal, or polymorphic encoding post-patch date. Correlate with CVE-2025-68686 threat feeds and known attacker ISPs.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism in FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline missed T1574.008 and filesystem-level persistence indicators entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system directories for symlink creation attempts, particularly targeting binary paths, library folders, or startup scripts. Alert on failed symlink operations indicating cleanup or rollback post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly typed as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' No hunt for lateral access to credentials, VPN configs, or firewall rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate abnormal egress from FortiOS appliances with known attacker C2 infrastructure used in CVE-2025-68686 campaigns. Flag access to admin credential stores, VPN configuration files, or encrypted traffic keys preceding outbound transfer.

suggestion.title: Prerequisite Filesystem-Level Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Two-stage attack requires hunting for the initial filesystem exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference with Fortinet security advisories to identify the likely prerequisite CVE for filesystem access. Hunt for evidence of binary modifications, privilege escalation attempts, or debug/diagnostic mode activation on FortiOS appliances preceding HTTP exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Post-Patch Evasion via Request Mutation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass of the patch via 'crafted HTTP requests.' Attackers will use mutation and polymorphism to evade post-patch signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-patch deployment, hunt for HTTP requests using encoding, chunking, case mutation, or parameter pollution against known symbolic link attack surface. Use behavioral detonation and sandboxing rather than signature-only detection.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2025-68686 as the exploitation vector and flags it as actively exploited in the wild (CISA KEV). Pipeline produced zero use cases and empty IOCs. A CRIT CISA KEV requires at minimum a vulnerability-scanning and exploitation-attempt detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests targeting known Fortinet FortiOS endpoints vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner output to prioritize systems running unpatched versions. Flag any systems with successful exploitation indicators (errors, timeouts, unusual responses) followed by post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Abuse on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states pipeline must 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—indicating T1547 post-compromise persistence. Pipeline generated no detection for this phase despite it being a core attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for creation or modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (config, startup, plugin paths). Establish baseline of legitimate symlinks. Alert on new or modified symlinks, especially if preceded by CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts or prior compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Patch-Bypass Attempts via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is explicit defense-evasion behavior (T1562). Pipeline supplied no corresponding detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify anomalous HTTP request patterns targeting FortiOS post-patch (after 2026-07-27): malformed headers, oversized payloads, header-injection attempts, path traversal variants, or repeated sequences that bypass standard controls. Correlate with patch-bypass indicators in FortiOS error logs or authentication-bypass successes.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Core impact stated as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline did not generate detection for information leakage or exfiltration from affected systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For FortiOS systems flagged by CVE-2025-68686 exploitation, monitor for bulk data transfers, unusual outbound connections, or anomalous DNS queries. Alert on exfiltration of configuration files, credentials, user/asset databases, or internal network segmentation data. Baseline normal FortiOS outbound traffic and flag statistical spikes.

suggestion.title: Detection of Preceding Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This indicates a two-stage attack. Pipeline did not address detection of the initial compromise, which is essential for full kill-chain visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference FortiOS systems vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 with other known exploited Fortinet vulnerabilities (e.g., pre-auth RCEs). Flag systems showing signs of prior compromise (e.g., unexpected file modifications, unauthorized access logs, unexpected processes) followed by CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Patch Compliance by Federal Due-Date

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK files with stripped or obfuscated class names, packed/compressed payloads, dynamic code loading from external sources, or mismatched signatures. Flag DEX files loaded at runtime from /tmp or app cache directories; legitimate apps rarely do this.

suggestion.title: Flying Eagle RAT Malware Signature Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Flying Eagle' as malware family. Pipeline failed to generate any IOC-based or signature-based detections. At minimum, known sample hashes/domains should be matched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create YARA/signature rules for Flying Eagle APK samples if hashes or package names are available in threat intel feeds. Cross-reference device event logs against malware repositories (APKCombo, VirusTotal, ANY.RUN). Alert on process execution matching known Flying Eagle process injection patterns or library loading sequences.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Run RAT When Imported Into Node.js'—indicating code execution via install scripts or require hooks during package load. Pipeline missed this entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process spawning from npm/node processes with unexpected parent relationships (e.g., child shell spawning network utilities). Flag install scripts that execute arbitrary binaries or spawn reverse shells. Correlate with npm install timing.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Network from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: RAT payload 'run when imported'—must establish C2. Pipeline missed C2 detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Node.js/npm processes for expected network destinations. Alert on connections to non-package-repo IPs/domains (e.g., outbound to dynamic IPs, non-standard ports, or known C2 infrastructure). Correlate with recent npm install.

suggestion.title: Known Compromised NPM Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'joyfill' packages as compromised. Pipeline should maintain and query IOC feed for package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install logs, package-lock.json, node_modules directory creation, and package manager output for known-bad package names or versions. Alert on installation from npm registry of packages on compromise feeds.

suggestion.title: RAT Process Behavior from NPM Context
suggestion.rationale: Payload explicitly identified as 'RAT'—classic post-exploitation behavior (process hollowing, credential stealing, file enumeration) should be detectable if running under Node.js parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for credential access APIs (lsass, SAM), file listing on sensitive paths, or process injection from Node.js child processes. RATs typically enumerate users, list directories, and exfil system info.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Detection—Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Two joyfill packages compromised—suggests either typosquatting, namespace confusion, or account takeover. Pipeline should flag package metadata discontinuities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for package version anomalies: sudden maintainer changes, new versions with suspicious code, package size inflation, or new dependencies added. Cross-reference against known registry mirror logs.

suggestion.title: goshs -b flag without colon separator (credential format validation bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is triggered by `-b 'admin:'` or empty-password config. A UC detecting malformed or semicolon/space-separated auth flags (non-standard syntax) could catch alternative bypass syntax not covered by current regex.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect goshs processes where -b flag syntax deviates from standard colon-delimited user:pass (e.g., spaces, multiple colons, escaped quotes). Capture command line for manual review.

suggestion.title: SFTP authentication accepted despite missing password field (auth state anomaly)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'SFTP accepts connections without password.' A UC correlating SFTP logon success with empty-credential config flags on the local process would directly detect exploitation.
log_sources: Sysmon (EventID 3: network connection + EventID 1: process with empty-cred flags
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SFTP session establishment (event logs or network state) with concurrent goshs process running -b flag without password segment. Low false-positive baseline in production environments.

suggestion.title: goshs version check for v2.1.3 (vulnerable release)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Start goshs v2.1.3 with -b ...' — version pinning is a precise hunting vector. Pipeline should extract version numbers from advisory text.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect goshs process execution where version string or help output can be extracted (e.g., from process command line, file properties, or parent execution logs). Correlate against known vulnerable versions from CVE database.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection use case was generated despite this being the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for unusual request patterns post-compromise: atypical HTTP methods, malformed headers, or requests targeting known patch-bypass paths. Baseline normal admin/API traffic; alert on deviations combined with 401/403 error spikes or symlink-related filesystem logs.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and patch bypass. No use case for detecting symlink manipulation was generated. Article states attacker needs 'filesystem level' access, implying auditable symlink creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation/modification in FortiOS directories, especially targeting startup, initialization, or script locations. Correlate with prior exploitation indicators. Look for symlink targets pointing outside expected paths or to world-writable locations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerability Assessment & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with federal patch deadline 2026-08-10. No vulnerability-scanning or asset-inventory use case was generated despite this being standard CISA KEV protocol (template references `<CVE>` substitution for vulnerability scanner matching).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all systems for Fortinet FortiOS instances with CVE-2025-68686 applied. Track patch date and compare against federal deadline 2026-08-10. Correlate non-patched instances with exposed internet-facing status and prior breach indicators to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Post-Compromise HTTP Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation *after* initial compromise via another vulnerability. Requires detection of anomalous HTTP behavior from already-compromised internal FortiOS devices; pipeline missed this multi-stage correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Fortinet instances flagged with prior-compromise indicators, monitor HTTP requests for: non-admin source IPs, unusual request rates, atypical User-Agent strings, or repeated failures followed by 200 responses. Baseline known-good admin activity; alert on divergence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Patch Rollback or Bypass Indicator Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' No detection for patch-integrity or rollback events. Implies audit log review for patch removal or version downgrades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Fortinet system with a prior-patched CVE-2025-68686 that reverts to an older firmware version, or logs indicating patch removal/bypass. Compare firmware version before/after exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Exposed Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can reach the vulnerability, implying exposed instances are the prerequisite. Template section explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' but no UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances (product field in config or HTTP headers) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Baseline: instances should be behind VPN/firewall; any with direct exposure are exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Crafted HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker exploits 'via crafted HTTP requests' to a 'symbolic link persistency mechanism.' No UC for HTTP-level exploitation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiOS management/API endpoints for anomalous patterns: requests targeting path traversal-like structures, symlink-related paths (e.g., containing '../' or symbolic-link operations), or requests from non-administrative source IPs. CVE-2025-68686 exploit traffic should show crafted payloads before persistence is set.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a post-exploitation persistence indicator the pipeline ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Fortinet FortiOS systems, detect creation or modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (cron, startup scripts, logging paths). Flag any symlink pointing to attacker-controlled executables or configuration files. Post-exploitation, symlinks are the mechanism for maintaining access across reboots.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Filesystem-Level Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level,' indicating multi-stage compromise. Pipeline missed detection for filesystem tampering or secondary exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious filesystem changes on Fortinet FortiOS instances: modifications to /usr/bin, /etc, /var/lib directories; unexpected binary execution with elevated privileges; or process spawning from unusual parent processes. These indicate preliminary compromise via secondary vulnerability before CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access in Fortinet FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—this data exfiltration or access is the ultimate impact but no detection use case was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated or unexpected access to Fortinet FortiOS configuration files, credential stores, or logs (e.g., syslog, diagnostic bundles). Correlate with outbound network activity to C2 infrastructure. Flag reads of /usr/local/bin, /etc/passwd-like files, or config exports by non-administrative processes.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'via crafted HTTP requests' against FortiOS and CISA KEV status means active exploitation. This is the primary attack vector and must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Fortinet FortiOS instances for request patterns associated with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation. Alert on requests bypassing known patches or targeting the symbolic-link persistency bypass. Correlate with asset inventory to identify exposed FortiOS endpoints.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information' post-compromise. Article implies configuration, credentials, or policy data may be accessible to attackers after initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual read access to FortiOS configuration files, certificate stores, or credential databases by system processes. Correlate with outbound network connections to external IPs. Flag if preceded by exploitation of other FortiOS CVEs.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic-Link Persistence Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases,' indicating adversary use of symlinks for maintaining access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan FortiOS filesystem for symbolic links created in startup paths, autoload directories, or system binaries. Monitor for process execution originating from symlinked file paths after exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance and Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-08-10. Article highlights patch-lag risk; rapid asset inventory and remediation tracking is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Fortinet FortiOS systems for CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Identify unpatched instances with exposure to untrusted networks. Flag instances past federal due date 2026-08-10 as critical priority and escalate for emergency patching.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies CVE-2025-68686 and directs analysts to 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' with this CVE substituted. Pipeline generated no vulnerability-scanning or asset-inventory UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system and FortiOS inventory for installations vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Flag unpatched systems and cross-reference against Federal remediation deadline (2026-08-10) to prioritize patching.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Symbolic Link Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence technique deployed after initial filesystem-level compromise. Pipeline failed to suggest filesystem-monitoring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For FortiOS systems with confirmed or suspected compromise, monitor filesystem for symbolic link creation/modification in system and config directories. Alert on symlinks with suspicious targets or creation timing correlating with exploitation signals.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation of FortiOS Post-Compromise

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For confirmed FortiOS compromises, hunt HTTP request logs for malformed or anomalous patterns targeting known vulnerable endpoints: unusual request methods, invalid headers, or payloads inconsistent with legitimate administrator activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Exposure from FortiOS

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Crafted HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' via 'crafted HTTP requests' targeting FortiOS; this is the primary initial access vector and most detectable phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiOS appliances for anomalous request patterns: malformed requests to admin endpoints (/admin, /system), missing User-Agent headers, unusual character encoding in paths, or requests from external IPs that precede authentication failures or file-system events.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all FortiOS instances and correlate against known-vulnerable versions. Alert on any unpatched instances; escalate post-due-date unpatched assets as critical.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system directories for symlink creation, especially targeting /bin, /lib, /var/www, or /opt. Alert when symlinks point outside expected FortiOS installation paths or when symlink events correlate with failed patch updates.

suggestion.title: Pre-Compromise Indicator Hunting on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'; detection must find evidence of that initial foothold.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthenticated Sensitive-Data Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS access logs for successful downloads or reads of sensitive files without corresponding authentication events. Flag API calls or file requests that bypass auth handlers or exploit known auth-bypass vectors.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Tracker

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Anomalies

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and bypass attempts; no file-system-level monitoring for symlink creation or manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symbolic link creation/modification in FortiOS application directories (/bin, /etc, /lib, /var) and in paths accessible post-exploit (temp, cache, backup directories). Correlate with prior filesystem-level compromise signals.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Service Restart and Patch Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass of 'patch developed for symbolic link persistency'; detection should cover instances where patched versions are re-exploited or service restarts occur in attack context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FortiOS service restarts (fortid, httpsd, etc.) occurring after HTTP requests matching the crafted-request pattern. Flag restarts within 5 minutes of anomalous file-system activity or unpatched version indicators.

suggestion.title: Multi-CVE Exploit Chain Detection (Filesystem Access → FortiOS Bypass)

suggestion.title: Abnormal HTTP Requests to FortiOS Interfaces

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation and Filesystem-Level Persistence

Alert on symlink targets pointing to sensitive files like credential stores, configuration files, or system binaries. Combine with privilege elevation events to identify post-exploitation persistence.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure from FortiOS

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploitation Chain Detection

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Pattern Detection for CVE-2025-68686

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify commits in public or high-dependency repositories that are no longer reachable from any branch but are tagged or referenced in CI/CD workflows. Flag rapid orphaning followed by tag reassignment.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiOS HTTP request logs for anomalous patterns targeting config endpoints, file paths, or symbolic link targets. Look for requests with path traversal, null-byte injection, or double-encoding. Correlate timing with known vulnerability disclosure date.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Mechanism Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Explicit persistence behavior post-compromise requiring filesystem monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symbolic link creation/modification on FortiOS systems (especially in /etc/init.d, config dirs). Timeline: correlate symlink events with preceding HTTP request anomalies and CVE-2025-68686 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure & Credential Access Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' following filesystem-level compromise. Describes data exfiltration phase of attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for bulk reads/exports of configuration files, credentials, VPN secrets, or certificates post-compromise (post-symbolic-link-modification). Baseline by user and time-of-day. Flag egress of large files or credential-pattern data to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploit Chain: Initial Compromise via First Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before exploiting this CVE. Implies prior vulnerability exploitation—detection must capture stage one.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate any FortiOS CVE vulnerabilities (pre-patch-date 2026-08-10) with subsequent anomalous behavior (HTTP, symlinks, credential access). Build exploit-chain timeline. Flag systems vulnerable to *any* FortiOS remote code execution as at-risk for multi-stage compromise via this chain.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Validation & Pre-Patch System Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article: patch developed to block symbolic link persistency; attacker crafts requests to bypass it. Implies verification that patch is applied and functioning before patch due-date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate all FortiOS instances are patched by 2026-08-10. For systems still vulnerable, hunt for HTTP request signatures that specifically target the symbolic link bypass (null-bytes, path encoding tricks, repeated 40x/50x responses). Cross-reference with exploitation timelines.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Fortinet FortiOS as the vulnerable product with CVE-2025-68686. Pipeline must scan for running FortiOS versions to enumerate exposure surface before the federal due date (2026-08-10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiOS instances in scope and cross-reference against CVE-2025-68686 CVSS data. Flag any instance older than the patched build as needing remediation. Splunk: index=vuln_scan vendor=Fortinet product=FortiOS | where version < patched_version | stats count by host, version, department.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Exploitation Attempts on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers exploit 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' after initial compromise. Pipeline must detect filesystem-level exploitation attempts that manipulate symbolic links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem activity for suspicious symbolic link creation or modification in critical directories (e.g., /bin, /lib, config paths). Alert on symlink traversal attempts that point outside their intended scope. Search for ln -s commands or CreateSymbolicLink API calls in FortiOS debug logs.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploit Bypass Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'bypass[es] the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline must detect malformed or anomalous HTTP patterns sent to FortiOS management interfaces post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS admin ports (typically 80, 443, 8080) containing suspicious payloads: oversized headers, malformed JSON, null-byte injection, or UTF-8 encoding anomalies. Correlate with POST requests to authentication endpoints or config-fetch URIs that appear immediately after credential compromise.

suggestion.title: Pre-Exploit Vulnerability Chaining Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline must detect the initial compromise vector before the symbolic-link / HTTP-bypass chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication attempts and known-exploit signatures against FortiOS to detect initial compromise activity. Look for unusual process execution, unexpected privilege escalation, or remote code execution patterns in the same timeframe as symbolic-link or HTTP anomalies.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' After compromise and patch bypass, attackers exfiltrate config, credentials, or secrets. Pipeline must detect abnormal access to sensitive FortiOS resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk read access to FortiOS configuration files (system.conf, etc.), VPN credentials, or API keys by compromised user accounts or unexpected system processes. Monitor for config backups or secret exports to attacker-controlled destinations (e.g., DNS exfiltration, HTTP POST to external IP).

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Remediation Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries mandate federal remediation by a specific due date (2026-08-10 in this case). Pipeline must track patching status and alert SOC leadership when due date approaches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated alerting: if any FortiOS instance remains unpatched for CVE-2025-68686 within 14 days of the federal due date, escalate to CISO. Splunk: index=patch_mgmt cve=CVE-2025-68686 status=unpatched | where daysUntilDueDate < 14 | alert.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Vulnerability Scanner Detection Post-Compromise

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning/probing of Fortinet appliances—version fingerprinting requests, CVE-specific payload tests, or reconnaissance of symlink paths. Alert on scanning followed by exploitation attempts within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Release Tag Manipulation on Critical Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the obfuscation technique enabling the attack, yet pipeline generated no detection for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect release tag creation or modification events that point to commits not reachable via primary branches. Alert when multiple version tags (v*, release-*) are rapidly re-pointed, especially to orphaned commits. Cross-reference tag move with branch deletion events to identify obfuscation pattern.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Software Supply Chain Repo
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies orphaned commits as 'one of the key enabling factors in exploiting the changes-files GitHub Action.' Attacker created a commit outside all branches specifically to hide it from normal visibility: 'commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits that become unreachable after branch deletion. Monitor for the pattern: branch creation → commit → branch deletion → orphaned commit remains accessible via direct URL. Flag especially in repositories with high dependency (e.g., GitHub Actions, package repos).

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Leaked to Plaintext in CI/CD Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core impact of the attack: 'attacker made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is the actual harm that must be detected to prevent data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs for patterns indicating encrypted secrets being decrypted and logged. Detect when secret environment variables appear in step output, echo commands, or error messages. Alert on logs containing decoded credential formats (JWTs, API keys, connection strings in plaintext).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Write Access or Privilege Escalation in Critical Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit.' The root cause is unknown ('As of this writing, it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions'), making detection of the access anomaly critical to early warning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new write-access grants to critical supply-chain repositories (high-dependency GitHub Actions, popular package repos). Alert on push events from unexpected or new user accounts. Monitor for permission escalation preceding malicious commits in repositories with 1000+ dependents.

suggestion.title: Unexpected External Network Calls from CI/CD Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack discovery mechanism: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections initiated from GitHub Actions jobs. Alert on unexpected external domains contacted during CI/CD runs, especially those not matching known build dependencies. Flag connections that exfiltrate data volumes inconsistent with normal artifact uploads.

suggestion.title: Version Tag Pointing to Unexpected Commit Hash
suggestion.rationale: Attack obfuscates using tag names (v35) that users trust, but pointing to malicious commits. Detection requires validating that release tags reference expected code. Article: 'GitHub tags are just convenient strings pointing to a particular commit - no magic.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate that semantic version tags match expected commit metadata (author, timestamp, parent commits). Alert when a version tag (v*, release-*) points to a commit with suspicious properties: orphaned state, unexpected authorship, no associated releases/milestones, or recent tag-pointer change.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Anomalous HTTP Requests

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS endpoints for HTTP requests with unusual payloads, unexpected headers, or malformed parameters targeting web interfaces. Correlate with CVE-2025-68686 presence in vulnerability scans. Alert on unauthenticated requests succeeding where they should fail.
