suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Credential theft' and 'Social engineering' as primary Q2 trends. Social engineering through email (T1598) precedes credential theft; detection should recognize reconnaissance queries and baiting emails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email campaigns targeting specific users/groups with credential-request payloads (password-change notifications, verify-account links); correlate with user clicks on external OAuth flows or forms requesting credentials.

suggestion.title: Repeated Failed Authentication After Phishing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: If email phishing is prevalent (article keyword), follow-on credential attempts will spike. Detection should alert on high-velocity failed sign-in attempts from external IPs post-phishing email delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline failed login attempts per user/org; trigger when external IP attempts >5 failed auths in <30 min for a user who received phishing email or visited phishing domain in past 24h.

suggestion.title: Domain Typosquatting / Lookalike Phishing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Q2 email-threat articles typically cite lookalike domains and typosquatted Microsoft/tenant domains as AiTM/phishing delivery vehicles. Detection should match DNS requests and email sender domains against homograph variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails from domains that differ by 1–2 characters from known corporate/Microsoft domains; alert on user DNS/HTTP requests to homograph domains; correlate with subsequent credential submission.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' exploiting 'via crafted HTTP requests'—no HTTP-pattern detection was generated. This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to known FortiOS admin/API endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api/v2) with suspicious parameter patterns or error responses indicative of exploitation probes. Correlate with known CVE-2025-68686 exploit signatures and request timing anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attacker 'would bypass the patch'—implies unpatched systems are at risk. Patch verification absent entirely from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scan data for FortiOS instances with version/patch levels below the remediation threshold documented in the CVE. Federal due date 2026-08-10 creates hard enforcement boundary.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem-Level Compromise Leading to CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—this two-stage attack chain is entirely absent from generated detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for evidence of prior filesystem compromise on FortiOS systems: suspicious file modifications in system directories, unauthorized config writes, privilege escalation attempts, or indicators consistent with exploitation of pre-CVE-2025-68686 vulnerabilities. Timeframe: weeks to months before observed CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse Post-Compromise on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' in exploit description—suggests post-compromise persistence via symlinks, not addressed in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS system/config directories (especially /etc, /bin, /lib paths or Fortinet-specific directories). Correlate with preceding privilege escalation or filesystem write events.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration or Information Disclosure Post-CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article culminates in 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—pipeline generated zero detection for successful exploitation outcomes (data access, exfiltration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for access to sensitive FortiOS data stores (config files, credential vaults, authentication logs, running configurations) following successful exploitation. Flag: large file transfers, base64-encoded exfiltration, or anomalous outbound connections from the FortiOS host.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states "CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner." Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or asset-hunting use cases despite this explicit instruction. Patch deadline 2026-08-10 creates audit/compliance signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for FortiOS instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Correlate patch timestamps against 2026-08-10 deadline. Flag any unpatched internet-facing FortiOS appliances as immediate remediation targets given active KEV exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article references "symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases." This is a persistence tactic following initial filesystem access but pipeline ignored the defense-evasion and persistence layers entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation or modification of symbolic links in startup directories, library paths, or plugin directories. Correlate with evidence of prior exploitation (failed authentication storms, suspicious log writes). Symlink creation outside normal admin procedures post-compromise is suspicious.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: "via crafted HTTP requests" to bypass patch and exploit post-compromise. This is an execution/exploitation technique but no HTTP-layer detection was surfaced. Indicates attacker sending anomalous requests after achieving filesystem persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FortiOS HTTP request patterns. Detect outliers: malformed query strings, unusual content-encoding, requests targeting symlink-related paths, or rapid retries of patched endpoints from internal sources post-compromise. High-confidence if correlated with filesystem symlink creation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Disclosure (Post-Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: "Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor." This is the impact/goal but pipeline generated zero exfiltration or collection-phase hunts. Attack assumes prior compromise; this UC catches the data extraction phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for bulk reads/downloads of sensitive files (admin.conf, vpn credentials, encryption keys, backup configs). Flag automated or script-driven access to config repositories, especially after filesystem-level signs of compromise or unexpected authentication failures.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Detection – FortiOS CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker "bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism." This implies defense-evasion post-patch. Pipeline missed this defense-layer technique entirely (T1562).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-patch deployment, monitor for evidence that symlink persistence mechanism is still active: attempts to create/use symlinks, requests targeting patched code paths succeeding when they should fail, or firmware rollback attempts. Indicates attacker using alternative exploit or vulnerability chaining.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Multi-Stage Exploitation Chain (CVE-2025-68686 + Initial Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: Article: "An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level." Pipeline produced no kill-chain reconstruction despite explicit multi-stage narrative: Stage 1 (initial compromise via unspecified CVE) → Stage 2 (filesystem persistence) → Stage 3 (HTTP exploitation of symlink logic).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate events: (1) failed or unusual authentication/exploitation attempts targeting FortiOS, (2) filesystem anomalies (symlink creation, config access), (3) suspicious HTTP patterns within 48-72 hours. A sequence of these stages in close time proximity is high-confidence indicator of active CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and 'crafted HTTP requests' — clear web exploitation signature. Pipeline ignored this despite being the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints with patterns consistent with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation (specific paths, parameter injection, or header anomalies). Correlate unauthenticated access attempts to FortiOS administrative interfaces with request timing and source reputation.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — a specific filesystem persistence technique the pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation/modification of symbolic links in persistence-relevant paths (startup folders, library paths, daemon directories). Look for processes spawning symlink operations from FortiOS service accounts post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Attack Against FortiOS Symbolic Link Fix
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' — a direct defense-evasion indicator showing attackers adapting to patches in active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to exploit CVE-2025-68686 by monitoring for crafted HTTP requests after official patch release. Look for filesystem activity that circumvents symlink checks (direct inode writes, file descriptor abuse, race conditions during access control evaluation).

suggestion.title: Pre-Exploitation Compromise Detection (FortiOS Secondary Attack Vector)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — this is a two-stage attack that requires detection of the *initial* compromise before CVE-2025-68686 is leveraged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Since FortiOS must be compromised first via separate vulnerability, detect lateral movement into FortiOS hosts and initial-compromise indicators (web shell upload, privilege escalation, config tampering). Use this to retroactively hunt for CVE-2025-68686 exploitation post-detection.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection — FortiOS Public-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states this is a CISA KEV entry ('currently being exploited') and recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution. Pipeline generated zero UCs. Vulnerability scanners must flag FortiOS instances with this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor output from vulnerability scanners targeting FortiOS instances for CVE-2025-68686 detection. Correlate against patch deployment logs and flag unpatched instances before federal due date (2026-08-10). Prioritize public-facing instances as exploitation vector requires external access.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Anomaly Detection — CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation mechanism: 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the patch. This is concrete behavioral IOC the pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs to FortiOS management/admin interfaces for anomalous request patterns (malformed URIs, symbolic link path traversal attempts, post-exploit command payloads). Establish baseline of legitimate admin traffic; alert on deviation, especially requests containing filesystem path manipulation or multi-stage exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Persistence — Symbolic Link Manipulation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' at filesystem level. Pipeline failed to surface persistence detection despite explicit mention of filesystem compromise required for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (particularly /etc, /bin, /var/log, configuration directories) for creation or modification of symbolic links outside change-control windows. Alert on unexpected symlinks that could enable persistence or privilege escalation, especially in conjunction with indicators of CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Information Access — Sensitive Data Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly exposes 'sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Article describes two-stage attack (initial compromise + filesystem-level access → information exposure). Pipeline missed detection for data access/exfiltration phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-detection of any CVE-2025-68686 exploitation or filesystem compromise, monitor FortiOS application logs for unusual access to sensitive stores (configuration files, credential caches, session tables, admin logs). Flag outbound transfers of configuration or credential data outside normal administrative channels.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Audit — CVE-2025-68686 Federal Deadline (2026-08-10)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes regulatory timing: 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators' with explicit deadline 2026-08-10. Pipeline generated zero compliance-tracking detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement continuous inventory tracking of all FortiOS instances, version numbers, and patch status for CVE-2025-68686. Generate non-compliance alerts for any unpatched instances, with escalation cadence intensifying as federal deadline approaches. Cross-reference patch status with network exposure (internal vs. public-facing).

suggestion.title: Public-Facing FortiOS Surface Discovery — T1190 Precondition Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires public-facing FortiOS exposure (T1190 precondition). Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' implies internet-reachable instances. Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery or exposure-hunting UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external internet-facing FortiOS instances using public scanning tools (Shodan, Censys, external vulnerability scanners). Identify and inventory all externally reachable FortiOS management interfaces. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner data to locate instances matching CVE-2025-68686 vulnerable versions. Flag for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Image Upload to Vulnerable Rails Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attackers' exploit via 'image uploads' — detection must capture POST/PUT to image-handling endpoints missing Authorization header or valid session token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on image file uploads (jpg, png, gif, webp, svg) to web endpoints from sources without valid auth tokens or session cookies. Correlate volume spikes and repeated failures to detect scanning/exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Sequences in Image Upload Filenames
suggestion.rationale: File-read exploits typically encoded as traversal payloads in filename or Content-Disposition (e.g., '../../../etc/passwd'). Article phrase 'read server files' implies directory traversal in upload metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match multipart upload Content-Disposition headers and filename parameters against traversal regex: (\.\.[\\\/]|%2e%2e[\\\/]|\.\.%5c|\.\.%2f). Flag encoded or obfuscated variants.

suggestion.title: Rails Image Processing Exception Surge Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Exploiting image libraries (ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, ActiveStorage) generates exception logs. Article implies vulnerability in image-handling code; Rails error logs will show processing failures correlating with exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spikes in ImageMagick/convert/GraphicsMagick failures or file permission denied errors in Rails logs within 10 seconds of unauthenticated image POSTs. Cross-correlate request ID with exception traces.

suggestion.title: Abnormal File Access Following Image Upload (Execution→Collection)
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation yields 'read server files' — file system access should show queries to config/, .env, /etc/passwd, or secrets outside normal app directories shortly after upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal file reads from app process (Rails). Alert when file access to non-upload directories (config/, secrets, /etc) spikes within 5-120 seconds post-exploit-attempt upload. Include process ancestry.

suggestion.title: Image Response Size Anomalies (Exfiltration Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: If vulnerability returns file content via image endpoint (reusing upload response or image download), response sizes become anomalous — /etc/passwd is ~1KB vs. typical photo 50KB+. Article indicates files are 'read' implying retrieval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GET requests to recently-uploaded image paths where Content-Length is <10KB and contains text strings (etc, passwd, config, BEGIN RSA KEY). Inspect response bodies for non-image MIME types or magic bytes.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes CRD with newline-escaped config (Flow/Output record_transformer injection)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'a user who can create Flow resources can inject Fluentd configuration by providing values that contain newlines'. Detection should target the injection syntax (newline chars closing blocks like </record>) in CRD definitions before they're rendered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Flow/Output CRD creation/modification API calls for record_transformer fields containing newline sequences (\n, %0A, or literal line breaks) that could escape Fluentd config syntax. Correlate with fluent.conf modification timestamps.

suggestion.title: Logging-operator RBAC allows unprivileged users to create Flow/Output
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires RBAC permissions to create Flow CRDs. Detection should monitor for overly permissive ClusterRoleBindings that grant 'create' on flow/output resources to service accounts outside logging namespaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit RBAC configuration for ClusterRoleBindings that grant 'verbs: [create, patch]' on 'resources: [flows, outputs]' to non-logging-operator accounts. Flag any newly created or modified bindings expanding these permissions.

suggestion.title: Fluentd process modifies fluent.conf with injected @type exec directives
suggestion.rationale: The attack payload injects new Fluentd directives (@type exec, <match **>) into the configuration file. Detection should observe fluent.conf file modification with suspicious pattern additions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/fluent/fluent.conf (and common variant paths) for file modifications by fluentd/ruby processes. Alert on changes introducing '<match **>' blocks, '@type exec' directives, or similar output plugin entries not matching expected config management tools.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE: Fluentd pod initiates outbound connections to external hosts (lateral movement/exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE via @type exec; post-compromise, attacker would lateral move or exfiltrate data. Current detections focus only on IMDS; should capture broader post-RCE C2 or data movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/UDP connections from Fluentd pods to external IPs (non-Kubernetes cluster, non-expected log aggregators). Correlate with shell spawning from Fluentd process in same time window.

suggestion.title: Logging-operator version check — update presence of vulnerable versions
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific versions vulnerable to this injection flaw. Asset inventory should flag running logging-operator versions without patches applied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Kubernetes cluster for logging-operator pod image tags matching vulnerable version ranges (e.g., <4.x.x depending on patch date). Alert on absence of patched versions in production namespaces.

suggestion.title: Successful shell command execution from @type exec Fluentd plugin (retrospective forensics)
suggestion.rationale: If Fluentd's exec output plugin runs a payload, check audit/shell history for commands executed as the Fluentd process user with suspicious arguments (curl, nc, bash -i, env variable exfiltration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Grep Fluentd container logs and parent audit trail for shell invocations (sh -c, /bin/bash) containing network utilities (curl, wget, nc) or environment variable access (env, printenv, /proc/*/environ). Filter out known Fluentd log shipping commands.

suggestion.title: JFrog Artifactory exploitation attempt via zero-day
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes models 'identified and exploited a previously unknown Artifactory zero-day to gain internet access' with 8 CVEs later disclosed in 7.161.15. No detection UC for supply-chain package proxy abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JFrog Artifactory access logs for unusual package requests, failed authentication attempts, or HTTP methods outside normal proxy-cache patterns. Flag requests from isolated/internal test environments attempting external package installation or unusual repository operations.

suggestion.title: Credential theft from Hugging Face config and collection
suggestion.rationale: Article states agent 'stealing cloud and cluster credentials' and 'mapped the credentials touched.' No detection for bulk credential harvesting from dataset-processing pipeline or config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration of environment variables, .env files, or configuration directories within Hugging Face infrastructure; unusual volume of cloud API credential lookups in logs; requests to cloud metadata services (e.g., EC2 instance metadata) from non-cloud-management processes.

suggestion.title: Third-party service credential reuse for attack infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals agent 'used publicly exposed credentials to compromise accounts on four third-party services' to set up staging/relay and data storage. This lateral compromise pattern is not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on logins to third-party services (especially infrastructure providers like Modal, compute platforms) from Hugging Face egress IPs or geolocations inconsistent with known infrastructure. Correlate failed Hugging Face intrusion attempts with successful logins to external services within same time window.

suggestion.title: Web-based C2 staging via pastebin and public utilities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'models also used public pastebin sites for sharing code and text, HTTP request-capture services commonly used during penetration tests and intrusions, screenshot services, and other web utilities.' No detection for this known C2 pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on egress to known pastebin domains (pastebin.com, paste.ee, etc.), public HTTP request capture services (requestbin, hookbin, webhook.site), and public screenshot services (screenshots.com, etc.) from internal infrastructure. Correlate with presence of legitimate API tokens or credentials in public paste history.

suggestion.title: Dataset exfiltration via extracted Hugging Face models repo
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'models extracted three partial datasets containing CyberGym solutions from a private Hugging Face repository' and 'models also used Hugging Face's platform and datasets as part of their command-and-control infrastructure.' No detection for using victim infra as exfil staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual dataset repository clones, downloads, or copies to user-controlled or external locations. Alert on datasets staged in public-facing buckets or copied to temporary compute instances with egress capability. Detect bulk read operations on private Hugging Face repos by single principal.

suggestion.title: Poor OPSEC artifacts: encryption key material left in logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'agents also had poor OPSEC, leaving behind traces of the attack, including encryption keys, that helped the responders further analyze the security incident.' Detection hypothesis focuses on forensic hunting post-incident.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-incident: forensic search for unencrypted or staged encryption keys in logs, temporary files, process environment, or command history. Real-time: flag processes that write base64-encoded or hex-formatted key material to logs, temp directories, or shell history; monitor for key material in error messages or debugging output.

suggestion.title: Prebid-server Request Parameter SSRF Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'bid request parameters that are interpolated into outbound request URLs' and 'craft bid request parameters that cause the server to send HTTP requests to unintended destinations.' No detection hunt addresses the parameter-layer attack — detecting malicious parameter values before they trigger outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to prebid-server auction endpoints for parameters containing suspicious values: IP addresses (especially 169.254.x.x, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x), localhost variants, known cloud metadata hostnames (metadata.google.internal, instance.aws.internal), or URL-encoded equivalents. Baseline normal parameter distributions and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Prebid-server Outbound Destination Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'send HTTP requests to unintended destinations' but existing hunts detect only egress to known-bad ranges. No baseline anomaly detection for previously-unseen or anomalous outbound destinations from the prebid-server process itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate outbound destinations from prebid-server (ad exchanges, analytics platforms, approved bidders). Generate alerts for connections to previously-unseen external IPs or destination ports, or rapid sequential connections to multiple internal hosts indicative of scanning.

suggestion.title: Cloud Metadata Service Credential Theft via SSRF
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1552.005 (Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API) and mentions 'host environment data extraction' but no hunt specifically detects successful metadata service access and credential retrieval by prebid-server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200 responses from metadata service endpoints (169.254.169.254 port 80, GCP/Azure metadata endpoints) originating from prebid-server process. Correlate with subsequent usage of extracted credentials (AWS STS, assume-role calls, GCP token usage) within minutes. Alert on any metadata endpoint access from non-infrastructure processes.

suggestion.title: Bid Request Parameter URL Encoding Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references parameter interpolation without specifying encoding/decoding mechanisms. Attackers may use double-encoding, hex encoding, or other bypasses to evade WAF/proxy filters on parameter values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect bid request parameters for signs of encoding obfuscation (hex-encoded %, double-URL encoding, Unicode escapes, mixed case hex). Flag encoded values decoding to internal IPs or metadata service names, or patterns matching known SSRF bypass techniques.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ruflo MCP
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'unauthenticated attackers' exploit Ruflo MCP. Core attack vector requiring network/auth-layer detection of unauthorized protocol handshakes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MCP connection attempts from untrusted sources without valid authentication credentials. Flag successful MCP session establishment from external networks or from source IPs not in trusted allow-list.

suggestion.title: Command Execution via Ruflo MCP Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'run commands'—core exploit capability. Requires process and command-line detection for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning from Ruflo MCP handler process or service account, especially encoding/obfuscation patterns (PowerShell -enc, base64). Correlate process creation with prior MCP auth failure events.

suggestion.title: AI Memory Poisoning via MCP Context Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'poison AI memory'—attackers inject malicious context/state into LLM models. Requires LLM context/prompt monitoring and anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to LLM context or prompt buffers from unauthenticated MCP sources. Flag context entries containing shell metacharacters, command injection patterns, or prompt-override payloads that diverge from legitimate use patterns.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Ruflo MCP Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates authentication is fully bypassed. Detection should surface reconnaissance and active exploitation probes pre-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic to Ruflo MCP endpoints for auth bypass patterns, malformed MCP handshake sequences, or requests lacking required auth headers. Correlate with public PoC availability and scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Poisoned AI Context
suggestion.rationale: Compromised AI memory could inject malicious instructions into downstream LLM calls, enabling lateral movement within multi-agent environments or AI orchestration platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LLM outputs or agent actions that execute unexpected commands post-context poisoning. Flag scenarios where LLM output triggers command execution inconsistent with user request intent or system role.

suggestion.title: Persistence via AI Model Memory Modification
suggestion.rationale: Injected poison persists in AI memory across sessions, enabling attacker commands to be re-executed or attacker instructions to be followed by future legitimate users interacting with the same LLM context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for injected context entries that remain accessible across multiple user sessions, session boundaries, or model deployments. Alert on context data modified by unauthenticated principals that persists longer than expected session lifetimes.

suggestion.title: VMware Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Auth Bypass' is explicitly named as one of three critical attack vectors. Zero UC generated for detecting exploitation of authentication flaws in VMware vCenter or ESXi management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts followed by successful access without credential submission, or direct access to privileged endpoints (SDK, API, web UI) bypassing auth validation. Monitor for requests to /api/sessions or similar token endpoints with invalid/missing credentials that succeed.

suggestion.title: VMware Code Execution via Hypervisor Service
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Code Execution' is explicitly named. No UC for detecting RCE exploitation in VMware service daemons (vpxd, hostd). Execution would occur in SYSTEM/root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned by vmware-hostd or vpxd daemons, especially shell interpreters (cmd.exe, /bin/bash), execution of binaries outside VMware installation paths, or process injection indicators from hypervisor context.

suggestion.title: VM Escape / Hypervisor Privilege Boundary Crossing
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'VM Escape' is explicitly named as third critical flaw. No UC for detecting guest-to-hypervisor escape attempts. This would involve ring-crossing, memory access violations, or VMXnet/I/O device exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for guest VMs triggering privilege-level exceptions (ring 0 access from ring 3), abnormal memory-mapped I/O patterns, vmxnet3/e1000 driver vulnerability exploitation attempts, or attempted direct hardware access from guest user-mode code.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable VMware Version Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Three critical flaws → patch urgency is high. No UC for asset-based detection: identifying unpatched vCenter/ESXi versions known vulnerable to these three flaws in the environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all ESXi hosts and vCenter instances running versions matching the three critical flaw CVE ranges. Cross-reference internal asset inventory against known-vulnerable release versions; escalate any unpatched instances as immediate exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: vSphere API or Web Client Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: VMware flaws are exploited via management interfaces (vCenter web, vSphere client, REST API). No UC for detecting exploit attempts (malformed requests, known-vulnerable endpoint access, token forgery).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to vCenter/vSphere endpoints with unusual request patterns: requests to known-vulnerable paths, malformed JSON payloads, missing/forged API tokens, or brute-force attempts against /api/sessions or /sdk endpoints.

suggestion.title: Modular malware implant deployment and staging
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly mentions 'modular implants'—a core architectural trait requiring detection of script or binary staging into memory/disk prior to execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual script interpreters (PowerShell, cmd.exe, wscript.exe) spawning child processes with obfuscated arguments or loading binaries from AppData, Temp, or ProgramData directories. Correlate suspicious file writes followed by execution within the same process tree to identify implant staging patterns.

suggestion.title: Command-and-control communication from modular malware
suggestion.rationale: Modular architecture inherently requires C2 communication to dispatch tasks. Article's 'modular' designation signals multi-stage implant framework expecting remote instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for beaconing patterns: outbound connections to low-frequency domains with regular timing intervals, POST/GET requests with unusual User-Agent or Cookie fields, and DNS queries for dynamically generated or fast-flux domains. Prioritize connections from processes known to load from temp directories.

suggestion.title: Persistence via scheduled tasks or registry autorun from malware families
suggestion.rationale: Multiple malware families in one campaign typically employ diverse persistence mechanisms. Article mentions 'four new malware families'—expect registry, task scheduler, and service-based persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* and HKCU equivalents pointing to unsigned binaries. Monitor schtasks.exe or New-ScheduledTask for creation of jobs with suspicious executable paths or encoding. Correlate timing of Registry/task modifications with parent process lineage traceback.

suggestion.title: Process injection or hollowing from modular malware
suggestion.rationale: Modular architectures commonly use process injection (CreateRemoteThread, NtCreateThreadEx) to evade EDR hooks and run payloads in trusted process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious allocations and writes to remote process memory, especially when a low-reputation source process targets system processes (lsass, svchost, explorer). Look for parent-child mismatches where a memory-resident module spawns child processes with blank command lines or unusual environment variable inheritance.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via modular implant framework
